CaseFacts External Benchmark Evaluation Across In-Corpus Precedent Verification (Track 1, $N=120$) and Modern Out-of-Corpus Refusal Control (Track 2, $N=50$). Evaluated under strict payload parity ($T=0.0$, 4096 tokens, LLaMA 3.3 70B) with independent non-LLaMA dual judges (\texttt{qwen3-next-80b-a3b} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}, 100.0\% concordance on parsed labels, zero fallback contaminations). Evaluates end-to-end citation fidelity directly in the synthesized completions. Panel A reports precedent citation recall, entity existence precision ($\text{CP}_{\text{entity}}$), doctrinal entailment precision ($\text{CP}_{\text{doctrinal}}$), and full-chain citation recovery on Category B. Panel B reports interactive relative markdown hyperlink attribution and piecewise epistemic negative containment across the 350-benchmark suite.}

Standardized External Benchmark Evaluation on a Stratified Sample of CLERC (Track 1, $N=120$) and TERRA-Specific Out-of-Corpus Refusal Stress Test (Track 2, $N=50$). Evaluated under strict payload parity ($T=0.0$, 4096 tokens, LLaMA 3.3 70B) with independent non-LLaMA dual judges (\texttt{qwen3-next-80b-a3b} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}, certified zero fallback contaminations). Citation metrics evaluate exact historical reporter matches parsed deterministically via \texttt{eyecite}, reporting Citation $F_1$ along with component Citation Precision (CP) and Citation Recall (CR). Safety evaluation is partitioned into the non-corpus caption share (a corpus-membership check, not a fabrication rate; see the notes below) and Doctrinal Misapplication Rate (disclosed under both Logical OR union and Unanimous AND judge concordance).}

Computational Budget Profiling, Sequential Pipeline Invocations, Stage Latency Breakdown, and Geometric Gate Calibration ($N=\numUniqueQueries$ Benchmark Queries Across \numComparativePipelines\ Comparative Architectures). Panel A reports total operations per query, active 70B generator calls, end-to-end and stage latencies (wall-clock ms), effective prompt/completion tokens, and modelled pipeline financial costs (token estimates at list prices, not metered). Panel B provides an \textit{ex-post} diagnostic evaluation of the Tier 2 geometric pre-filter ROC manifold ($\text{AUROC} = \TerraGateIsolatedAUROC$) across the 20,000-case index; the operational threshold $\tau=\IssueTwentyFourDistThreshold$ was frozen prior to benchmark construction and evaluation.}
Complete Pre-Specified Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) Hypothesis Testing Family ($M=20$ Tests Across 4 Baselines $\times$ 5 Evaluation Slices).}

Obscure Overruled Precedent Benchmark Evaluation ($N=\ObscCohortSize$ Obscure Decisions, $N=\ObscKappaCleanEvals$ Completion Instances) and Cross-Suite Descriptive Contrast with Famous Landmark Decisions ($N=\ObscFamousCohortSize$ Category D Precedent Queries). Evaluated under strict payload parity with two distinct LLM judges (\texttt{qwen3-next} and \texttt{gpt-oss}, $\kappa = \ObscKappa$; unverified quotes flagged: \ObscQwenUnverifiedQuotes{} and \ObscGptOssUnverifiedQuotes{}). Panel A reports fine-grained outcome distributions across four evaluation arms. Panel B reports preregistered paired hypothesis tests, sequential gate enforcement, and sensitivity subsets. Panel C reports a descriptive cross-suite contrast comparing parametric performance on famous versus obscure overruled precedents. Panel D reports per-judge robustness distributions and primary paired test sensitivity.}

Comprehensive Per-Category Epistemic and Safety Refusal Breakdown Across All 350 Benchmark Queries ($N=1,750$ Evaluations), Alongside Audited Category D Adversarial Deception Multi-Class Robustness Breakdown ($N=75$ Queries).}

Direct Evidence Retrieval Quality, Chain-Length Recovery, and Hyperparameter Robustness Grids on Category B ($N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ Queries, $\CatBGoldPrecedents$ Gold Landmark Precedents). Evaluated decoupled from the generator on retrieved context subgraphs delivered prior to generator invocation. Panel A reports overall precedent recovery across comparative retrievers. Panel B disaggregates precedent discovery by evolutionary chain length (3, 4, and 5 nodes; spanning 2, 3, and 4 citation hops). Panel C reports retrieval hyperparameter robustness sweeps: Section 1 evaluates the primary grid under the historical pre-Issue \#13 engine (exact 100/100 parity reproduction of the published baseline), while Section 2 reports the bounded post-Issue \#13 engine as an operational-efficiency diagnostic (35k char / 40-node limits).}

Standalone Traffic Cop Query Intent Classifier Evaluation Across Canonical Benchmark Queries ($N=\RouterTotalQueries$), and Category-Disaggregated Routing Behavior with Downstream Defense-in-Depth Outcomes. Evaluated with Google Gemma 3 12B Instruction-tuned (\texttt{\RouterModel}) at $T=0.0$ under structured Pydantic schema validation (\texttt{RoutingDecision}). Panel A reports the $2 \times 2$ standalone binary confusion matrix (EASY: single-point factual lookup; HARD: multi-hop evolutionary, out-of-domain, or adversarial query), classification metrics, and inference latency percentiles. Panel B disaggregates routing decisions across benchmark categories (A, B, C, D) with a self-verifying total row ($110 + 240 = 350$), confirming that overall benchmark safe handling reaches \RouterOverallSafeHandlingRate\ (348/350), with 100.0\% of misrouted Category D queries neutralized downstream without fatal error.}
Sensitivity Analysis: Certified Clamped Faithfulness vs. Pre-Clamp Raw Judge Scores Across All 350 Benchmark Queries ($N=1,750$ Evaluations) Under the Canonical V2 Dual-Judge Protocol.}

Temporal Parametric Leakage Stress Test ($N=50$ historical queries across five SCOTUS temporal cutoffs $T=1890$ to $1980$). Panel B provides full discordant-pair $(b, c)$ transparency across complete cases ($N_{\text{cc}}$) and bounded missing-data envelopes ($N=50$) under exact McNemar testing.}

Evaluates standalone BFS citation traversal seeded by benchmark origin precedents ($s = q[\texttt{target\_nodes}][0]$) traversing all available directed graph edges (generic \texttt{CITES}); strictly decoupled from end-to-end vector retrieval and live index upsert. Latency reflects in-memory NetworkX traversal (grand median $\IssueNineteenBFSLatencyMedianMs$~ms, mean $0.15 \pm 0.18$~ms; 54/106 queries complete in $1$--$3\,\mu\text{s}$ while 52/106 expand denser neighborhoods in $0.1$--$0.6$~ms).}

\title{Unifying Event Evolution Graphs and Reasoning Traces via Semantic Entailment: A Dual-Phase Architecture for Judicial GraphRAG}

The bottleneck arises with continuous knowledge drift and multi-step reasoning. Static vector indices can accumulate conflicting, time-stamped versions of the same fact; a retriever ranking by semantic similarity may surface several together, leaving a frozen generator without a basis for choosing the chronologically authoritative one and prone to state outdated law. For multi-step derivations, similarity-based pipelines can retrieve fragments that omit precedential and doctrinal dependencies. We motivate the design with these mechanisms and do not measure them in isolation.

Recent work addresses these bottlenecks in silos. Graph-based retrievers organize facts chronologically but lack the procedural logic to guide multi-hop generation; retrieval of intermediate reasoning traces improves deduction but is temporally blind and mostly confined to mathematics or coding; and corrective Agentic RAG frameworks rely on retrieval evaluators that may not capture conceptual relevance, as a SHAP-based study of the CRAG T5 evaluator found it relies mainly on named-entity alignment rather than semantic similarity \cite{yalavarthi2026opensourcereproductionexplainabilityanalysis}. Many hybrid systems route among a small fixed set of channels, while adaptive multi-strategy routing is emerging \cite{hashmi2026adaptivequeryroutingtierbased}.

We therefore introduce a dual-phase GraphRAG architecture for evolving, knowledge-intensive domains (traversal stability under temporal snapshot expansion is evaluated in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}). All heavy computation is offline, building a dual-index corpus that cross-links an Event Evolution Graph (EEG), which encodes precedent relationships across \CorpusTotalOpinions\ judicial decisions and \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed citation edges, with a node-level procedural trace scaffold, a fixed five-step template instantiated per case. Online, a small language model acts as a Traffic Cop router classifying each query as EASY or HARD, selecting a fast path or citation-graph traversal, which yields a bimodal execution profile (gross median \TerraFastPathMedianSeconds~s on Category~A factual lookups vs.\ \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds~s on Category~B multi-hop chains). Before generation, an LLM-prompted entailment grader decides whether the retrieved evidence suffices; its accuracy was not independently validated.

We compare TERRA with four baselines, including Direct LLM and Flat Vector RAG, on a \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark with a 35-query pilot ablation. We did not test attention dilution or context-length effects directly, and TERRA's mean retrieved context is longer than the retrieval baselines' (about 18{,}400 versus 2{,}900--4{,}100 characters). In a 50-query temporal leakage probe, TERRA did not leak less than Flat Vector RAG under default prompting (the preregistered hypothesis $H_1$ is not supported, and Flat RAG refused 23 of 50 queries) but gave more historically correct answers (\TerraGatedHlcrA{} versus \FlatRagHlcrA{}). The work is an experimental research framework for context fidelity in temporal legal AI on historical SCOTUS jurisprudence.

To supply that logic, recent work augments retrieval with intermediate reasoning trajectories. CoT-RAG \cite{li2025cotragintegratingchainthought} combines knowledge-graph-guided chain-of-thought generation with retrieval and reports gains of $4.0\%$ to $44.3\%$ across nine public reasoning datasets, and surveys of agentic reasoning \cite{lin2025comprehensivesurveyreinforcementlearningbased, liang2025reasoningrag12} describe pipelines in which agents identify knowledge gaps and generate intermediate traces to inform search. Legal benchmarks include CaseHOLD \cite{zheng2021casehold}, which evaluates holding identification, and CLERC \cite{hou2024clerc}, which evaluates U.S. case retrieval and analysis drafting; as we read them, neither targets superseded or overruled authority, the gap TERRA's evaluation addresses. LegalBench \cite{guha2023legalbench} broadens coverage to 162 tasks across six types of legal reasoning. Earlier legal NLP work includes outcome prediction for Supreme Court cases \cite{katz2017general} and domain-pretrained language models such as LEGAL-BERT \cite{chalkidis2020legalbert}, and an audit of leading commercial legal research tools found that they hallucinated in more than 17\% of queries \cite{magesh2025hallucination}. Trace-retrieval frameworks have been evaluated mainly on quantitative domains or static statutory collections, leaving longitudinal common-law settings largely untested.

Query routers and evaluators form the connective tissue of the pipeline. Hashmi \cite{hashmi2026adaptivequeryroutingtierbased} highlighted the rigidity of single-channel retrieval and introduced an Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval framework, noting that pure vector similarity often fails to capture structural navigation. Yalavarthi \cite{yalavarthi2026opensourcereproductionexplainabilityanalysis} found through SHAP analysis that the T5-based evaluator in Corrective RAG (CRAG) prioritizes named-entity matching over semantic understanding and transfers poorly to scientific questions. Putta et al. \cite{putta2026casefactsbenchmarklegalfactchecking} showed with CaseFacts that unrestricted web search degrades legal fact-checking relative to closed-book baselines. Retrievers ranking by lexical or embedding similarity can return overruled precedents alongside current ones without marking which was overturned, which motivates the explicit entailment check tested below.

To our knowledge, no system reviewed in Section~\ref{sec:related-work} unifies temporal precedent management, node-level procedural trace retrieval and semantic-entailment evaluation in one pipeline: graph models track chronology but lack procedural logic, trace models enhance reasoning but lack temporal awareness, and many routers select among a few retrieval channels. TERRA cross-links a temporal EEG with a node-level trace database, retrieving each precedent node with its fixed five-step trace scaffold; it uses an LLM-prompted entailment grader in place of an entity-alignment evaluator and a binary Traffic Cop router choosing between a fast path and citation-graph traversal. This dual-phase design targets continuous knowledge drift (examined under snapshot expansion in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}) and multi-hop reasoning without retraining the foundation model.

TERRA (Temporal-Evolution and Reasoning-Trace RAG) is designed as a two-phase, closed-loop GraphRAG architecture for temporal legal reasoning on historical common-law jurisprudence. The core engineering philosophy strictly separates offline corpus ingestion and knowledge structure construction from online query routing and inference. This separation ensures that all computationally intensive graph traversals, citation link extractions, and reasoning trace generations are performed offline, maintaining responsive online inference with a bimodal latency profile (median \TerraFastPathMedianSeconds~s on factual lookups vs. \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds~s on multi-hop citation chains; Figure~\ref{fig:system_architecture}).

\subsection{Phase 1: Offline Ingestion and Knowledge Graph Construction}
\label{subsec:phase1-ingestion}

\subsubsection{Authentic Judicial Opinion Corpus (\CorpusTotalOpinions\ Cases)}
TERRA operates on \CorpusTotalOpinions\ full-text Supreme Court opinions spanning \CorpusTemporalSpan\ (Volumes 50--448), curated from an initial harvest of 23,010 public-domain federal decisions from CourtListener and the Harvard Caselaw repositories (public domain under 17 U.S.C. \S~105). To remove non-precedential noise, opinions were filtered by length ($\text{character count} \ge 4{,}000$). Of the \IssueTwentyTotalDecisionsScanned\ decisions in \IssueTwentyTotalVolumesScanned\ scanned U.S. Reports volumes, \IssueTwentySubFiveHundredCharCount\ (\IssueTwentySubFiveHundredCharPct) are shorter than 500 characters (procedural orders, summary dispositions and docket records, subject to audit). The length filter nevertheless induces bias: it excludes \IssueTwentyIntermediateExcludedCount\ intermediate decisions ($500$--$3{,}999$ characters, \IssueTwentyIntermediateExcludedPct), of which \IssueTwentyIntermediatePageRankGeNinetyNineFive\ rank in the top $0.5\%$ of citation authority under Harvard CAP PageRank (e.g., \textit{Haines v. Kerner}, \textit{Dusky v. United States}, \textit{Lucas v. Earl}, \textit{Sipuel v. Board of Regents}, \textit{Gayle v. Browder}). The corpus contains no synthetic cases. A core set of 34 landmark civil rights decisions, from \textit{Dred Scott v. Sandford} (1857) through \textit{Plessy v. Ferguson} (1896), \textit{Missouri ex rel. Gaines v. Canada} (1938) and \textit{Brown v. Board of Education} (1954) to \textit{Swann v. Charlotte-Mecklenburg} (1971), anchors the multi-hop benchmark.

\subsubsection{Citation Parsing and Directed Edge Classification}
Citations are extracted with \texttt{eyecite}~\cite{cushman2021eyecite}, a token-level extraction and reporter-normalization utility that establishes citation existence ($A \xrightarrow{\text{CITES}} B$) without inferring precedential treatment or approval; strings are normalized via \texttt{cite.corrected\_citation()} (e.g., \snippet{347 U.S. 483}) and matched to opinion identifier hashes. The verified Event Evolution Graph has \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed edges (\IssueTwentyOneTotalCitesEdges\ \texttt{CITES} and \IssueTwentyOneOverrulesEdges\ \texttt{OVERRULES}), with forward chronological validity at calendar-year granularity and zero cross-year violations (\IssueTwentyOneCrossYearViolationsPct); \IssueTwentyOneSameYearEdges\ edges (\IssueTwentyOneSameYearEdgesPct) link same-year opinions, including \IssueTwentyOneIntraYearReversals\ intra-year reporting artifacts. An earlier ``99.91\% chronological validity'' claim has unresolved provenance (likely a decimal approximation of full-date ordering, $\IssueTwentyOneStrictlyPriorDateEdges/\IssueTwentyOneTotalCitesEdges = {}$\IssueTwentyOneStrictlyPriorDatePct). A reproducible stratified audit across 14 decades ($N=\IssueTwentyOneAuditSampleN$, seed \IssueTwentyOneAuditSeed) confirms verbatim citation presence in \IssueTwentyOneAuditCitationPresentPct\ of sampled edges (95\% CI: \IssueTwentyOneAuditCitationPresentCI), with \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedPct\ verified direct reliance (95\% CI: \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedCI) and \IssueTwentyOneAuditQuotationPct\ citations inside third-party quotations.

The \texttt{OVERRULES} edges are typed relations taken from a Wikipedia mirror of the Congressional Research Service (CRS) report R45319 and resolved to corpus nodes by citation and name matching ($A \xrightarrow{\text{OVERRULES}} B$: $B$ overruled in whole or in part by $A$). We audited all \IssueTwentyOneOverrulesEdges\ tagged edges against the overruling opinions: 3 (\textit{Edelman}$\to$\textit{Wyman-Gordon}, \textit{Griffin}$\to$\textit{Frisbie}, \textit{Hensley}$\to$\textit{Norwood}) were mis-resolved by the first-party-name fallback when the intended target was absent from the 20k corpus, and the other 53 are consistent in case identity, although the scope of each overruling (full or partial) was not legally adjudicated. None of the 3 was serialised in any of the 32 deployed contexts that contained an \texttt{OVERRULES} line, but indirect effects on retrieval or ranking cannot be excluded: replaying the current traversal code on both graphs gave identical outputs for 159 recorded traversals, but the code version used in the runs was not pinned. All reported results use the frozen index; a corrected derivative without the 3 edges (145,363 edges; SHA256 \texttt{14827bd6...}) is released in the replication bundle as a separately versioned file and is not used by any reported run. The 19 Category-D queries (e.g., \textit{Brown} invalidating \textit{Plessy}) cover 9 distinct \texttt{OVERRULES} edges, all among the 53 consistent ones (Section~\ref{subsec:benchmark-design}). The graph is serialized as a NetworkX \texttt{DiGraph} (\texttt{dataset\_20k\_cap/terra\_eeg\_index\_20k.json}).

To check evidence integrity, we audited all \TraceTotalNodes\ nodes. Substring verification against raw CAP casebody JSON gives an aggregate span grounding rate of \TraceSpanGroundingRate\ (\TraceSpanGroundingCount\ exact matches) against the pre-registered $\ge \TraceSpanGroundingThreshold$ floor, with \TraceSpanDiscrepanciesCount\ discrepancies (\TraceSpanDiscrepanciesPct) attributable to short per curiam docket orders lacking opinion text in CAP. A dual-critic factual-consistency and temporal-anachronism audit over an $N=\TraceAuditSampleCount$ cohort (a complete census of the curated landmark prototypes in the graph, $N=\TraceCuratedCensusCount$, with 3 short per curiam orders omitted by CAP's $\ge 4{,}000$-character filter, plus a stratified random sample of the procedural majority, $N=\TraceStratifiedProcCount$ across seven categories) confirmed \TracePopWeightedAnachronismFreePct\ population-weighted temporal integrity (no cited precedent post-dates its target; $\text{decision\_date}(\text{precedent}) \le \text{decision\_date}(\text{target})$) and \TracePopWeightedFactualPct\ factual consistency. These figures do not show case-specific reasoning quality: the scaffold asserts no case facts beyond title and year, and the curated-prototype census cannot be reproduced from the evaluated index. Provenance tags, prompts and ledgers (\texttt{docs/REASONING\_TRACE\_SPECIFICATION.md}) are not yet released.

\subsection{Phase 2: Online Query Routing and Inference Engine}
\label{subsec:phase2-inference}

A \textit{fatal constraint violation} is a response that affirms an overruled doctrine, misattributes controlling constitutional authority or adopts a legally impossible premise from an adversarial prompt (Category~D); a \textit{false refusal} is an unwarranted refusal of an in-domain Category~A lookup whose controlling precedent is present and unambiguous.
We analyze the pre-built dual-index corpus for composition, topology and centrality.

To audit the taxonomy without manual labelling, we evaluated a stratified sample of $N=\IssueTwentyTwoTotalSampleN$ opinions (\IssueTwentyTwoBaselineSampleN\ baseline and \IssueTwentyTwoEdgeSampleN\ edge cases: \IssueTwentyTwoTieSampleN\ ties, \IssueTwentyTwoMultiTagSampleN\ multi-tag, \IssueTwentyTwoFallbackSampleN\ fallback; seed \IssueTwentyTwoSamplingSeed) with two automated, model-distinct evaluators: Judge~A, a deterministic statutory/constitutional parser over opinion texts and headnotes, and Judge~B (\texttt{databricks-gpt-oss-120b} with logged fallback to \texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct}; zero LLaMA calls). Raw agreement was \IssueTwentyTwoIEARawAgreement\ (Cohen's $\kappa = \IssueTwentyTwoIEACohensKappa$). Disagreements and edge cases went to a third automated adjudicator, Judge~C (\IssueTwentyTwoAdjudicatorModel), blinded to the taxonomy and prior votes, with zero endpoint overlap with Judge~B (\IssueTwentyTwoAdjudicatorOverlapCount/\IssueTwentyTwoTotalSampleN). This is automated model adjudication, not human legal-expert validation. Against this reference, the primary-domain taxonomy has a Horvitz-Thompson prevalence-weighted accuracy of \IssueTwentyTwoHorvitzThompsonAccuracy\ (SE: \IssueTwentyTwoHorvitzThompsonSE, 95\% CI: \IssueTwentyTwoHorvitzThompsonCI); over the \IssueTwentyTwoTotalSampleN\ cases, \IssueTwentyTwoStrictCoherentPct\ (\IssueTwentyTwoStrictCoherentCount) are strictly coherent, \IssueTwentyTwoPartialCoherentPct\ (\IssueTwentyTwoPartialCoherentCount) partially aligned, for a substantively grounded rate of \IssueTwentyTwoSubstantivelyGroundedPct\ (\IssueTwentyTwoSubstantivelyGroundedCount), and \IssueTwentyTwoIncoherentPct\ (\IssueTwentyTwoIncoherentCount) incoherent. In the edge strata, ties reached \IssueTwentyTwoTieAccuracy\ coherence, multi-label tagging \IssueTwentyTwoMultiTagPrecision\ precision and \IssueTwentyTwoMultiTagRecall\ recall (F1 \IssueTwentyTwoMultiTagFOne), and the fallback \IssueTwentyTwoFallbackValidityPct\ validity as an unkeyed default.

\noindent\textbf{Task Scope vs.\ Background Corpus.} The EEG covers the full \CorpusTotalOpinions-case docket across seven areas (including \CorpusPrivateLawOpinions\ Substantive Private Law and \CorpusGeneralConstitutionalOpinions\ General Statutory decisions; Table~\ref{tab:corpus_stats}), but Category~B concentrates on constitutional and federal public-law trajectories (20 queries each across Civil Rights, Criminal Procedure, First Amendment, Commerce Clause and Administrative Law; \IssueTwentyFiveCatBConstitutionalPublicPct). Of the \IssueTwentyFiveBenchInDomainTotal\ in-domain queries (Categories~A, B and D), \IssueTwentyFiveBenchConstitutionalPublicCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchConstitutionalPublicPct) are constitutional or public law, \IssueTwentyFiveBenchPrivateLawCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchPrivateLawPct) private law and \IssueTwentyFiveBenchGeneralStatutoryCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchGeneralStatutoryPct) general statutory. Private-law disputes were not modeled as 3--5 node citation chains, whereas constitutional jurisprudence shows longitudinal evolution and explicit overruling; retaining the full repository gives a high-distractor environment where constitutional reasoning must avoid \IssueTwentyFiveCorpusCombinedPrivateStatutoryPct\ commercial and statutory background nodes.

\noindent\textbf{Category~C and D Construction.} The 75 Category~C queries were pre-registered across five domains (Subtypes C1--C5) before evaluation, and an automated audit against the indexed repository found 0/75 title, citation or holding overlaps. The 75 Category~D queries were built by the research team under a pre-registered taxonomy: D1 ($N=19$) explicit overruled-precedent traps, D2 ($N=19$) title substitution, D3 ($N=19$) temporal inversion with a $\ge 5$-year gap, and D4 ($N=18$) procedural-posture deceptions, sampled with \texttt{RANDOM\_SEED = 42} from 19 verified doctrine-invalidation pairs. All queries were locked into \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json} (SHA256: \texttt{8144fa81...}) before any pipeline ran, with no queries or references indexed into ChromaDB (Section~\ref{subsubsec:data-leakage}); the domain-labeling protocol and Category~C catalog are published in supplementary documentation. A standalone 15-query stress test (10 out-of-context, 5 adversarial; \texttt{stress\_test.py}) checks firewall boundary consistency.

\enlargethispage{3\baselineskip}
\paragraph{Obscure Overruled Precedent Suite.} To test whether Category~D safety reflects retrieval or memorization of famous landmarks, we built a supplementary suite of \ObscCohortSize\ obscure overruled-precedent queries from the 47 CRS \texttt{OVERRULES} edges not used in Category~D, excluding three whose overruling opinions never mention the target (we infer, without a retained exclusion ledger, that these are the three mis-resolved edges of Section~\ref{subsec:phase1-ingestion}) and selecting the thirty lowest-in-degree pairs by a mechanical rule fixed before inference. Each query asks what the overruled decision held without hinting at the overruling authority (leakage audited). Four arms ran under identical settings: Direct LLM; Flat Vector RAG with the identical instruction block; Full TERRA; and TERRA-Unlabeled, which removes the relation tags, the overruling heading, the prompt's reference to the tag and the enlarged excerpt allocation for overruling edges while keeping seeds, traversal and router unchanged. Two judges (Qwen3-Next-80B, GPT-OSS-120B; neither is the generator) classified each answer as refusal, verified refutation, fatal error (affirmed as current law, or recited without warning) or hedge, and the combined class takes the more severe judgment. The primary hypothesis, sensitivity subsets and cross-suite contrast were preregistered before any live output; for the contrast we re-ran the nineteen Category~D doctrine-invalidation queries under identical code, prompts and judges.

\noindent\textbf{Baseline Implementation Details and Adaptation Rigor.} All five pipelines share the generator \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} ($T=0.0$, max tokens~4,096), programmatic payload assertions (identical model, temperature, token limit) and the 350-query benchmark \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json} (SHA256: \texttt{8144fa81...}) over the 20,000-case Harvard CAP corpus. The historical 1,750-run benchmark used index \texttt{terra\_eeg\_index\_20k.json} (SHA256: \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalCorpusHashShort}, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalFileSizeMB~MB), whereas the active post-Issue~\#6 index is SHA256 \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCorpusHashShort} (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveFileSizeMB~MB), satisfying $\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges + \IssueTwentyThreeCrsAddedEdges = \IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges$ (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCites\ \texttt{CITES}, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveOverrules\ \texttt{OVERRULES}; \IssueTwentyThreeReclassifiedEdges\ historical \texttt{CITES} edges were retyped as \texttt{OVERRULES}, which preserves the count, and 3 edges were CRS-added, all 3 of which the audit found mis-resolved; without them the graph has 145,363 edges, 145,310 \texttt{CITES} and 53 \texttt{OVERRULES}). Of the 20,000 opinions, \IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsCount\ have substantive extracted holdings (\IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsPct; \IssueTwentyThreeTierOneHeadnotesCount\ syllabus headnotes, \IssueTwentyThreeTierTwoRegexCount\ regex statements), \IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackCount\ (\IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackPct) rely on preamble fallbacks, and \IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingCount\ holding fields are non-empty (\IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingPct; \IssueTwentyThreeUnpopulatedHoldingCount\ unpopulated). Graph representations differ by architecture: GraphRAG-Adapted partitions an undirected citation network (\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGUndirectedEdges\ edges) by NetworkX Louvain modularity ($Q=\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGModularity$, resolution 1.0, seed 42; chosen over C-based Leiden for host build constraints); HippoRAG-Adapted runs Personalized PageRank ($\alpha=0.85$, tolerance $10^{-6}$, max 50 iterations, top-$k=5$) over a symmetric citation matrix (\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGNonZeroEntries\ entries); and TERRA traverses the directed chronological graph by BFS ($k=2$, $d=2$, hub cap 50, $d_{L2} \le 1.3$). Context ceilings are character-based (\texttt{[:N]}): Flat RAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeFlatCharCeiling, GraphRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGCharCeiling, HippoRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGCharCeiling\ and TERRA \IssueTwentyThreeTerraCharCeiling\ characters, an intentional $\IssueTwentyThreeContextAsymmetryRatio$ ceiling-to-ceiling asymmetry (\IssueTwentyThreePromptTokenRatio\ prompt tokens, Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget}); realised mean context was $18{,}404$ characters for TERRA versus $3{,}141$ for Flat RAG ($5.9\times$), a confound. The judging prompt applies a \IssueTwentyThreeJudgeMiddleOmissionCeiling-character middle-omission split (\texttt{[:25000]} + \texttt{[-25000:]}), covering 100\% of baseline context ($<6{,}000$ characters) while preserving TERRA's initial seeds and terminal citing authorities. Finally, the baseline adapters include post-hoc amendments rather than frozen pre-registration: Amendments~F and G (HippoRAG regex and GraphRAG formatting fixes) and K, L and M (judge JSON parse clamping, refusal string harmonization, fast-path ground-truth floor).

We first dissect the architecture through an ablation, then evaluate multi-hop evolutionary reasoning via pairwise win rates and faithfulness, examine factual precision and safety across the \numTotalEvals-evaluation benchmark, profile stage latencies, and conduct significance and power audits.

\subsection{Multi-Hop Evolutionary Reasoning and Pairwise Win Rates (Category B)}
\label{subsec:evolutionary-reasoning}

Category~B tracks constitutional doctrine across multi-decade precedent arcs (e.g., \textit{Plessy} (1896), \textit{Gaines} (1938), \textit{Sweatt} (1950), \textit{Brown} (1954)). Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance} gives comparative performance and head-to-head win rates over $\CatBTotalPairs$ paired evaluations.

TERRA's Category~B faithfulness exceeds Flat Vector RAG by $\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGDelta$ (paired Wilcoxon $q=\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGAdjQ$; the bootstrap CI of the mean difference, [$\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGBootCILow$, $\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGBootCIHigh$], includes zero while the Hodges--Lehmann median difference, $\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGHLMedian$ [$\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGHLLow$, $\CatBTerraVsFlatRAGHLHigh$], does not), HippoRAG by $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ ($q=\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGAdjQ$, $d_z=\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDz$) and GraphRAG by $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$ ($q=\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGAdjQ$). TERRA wins $\TerraVsFlatRAGCatBWins$, $\TerraVsGraphRAGCatBWins$ and $\TerraVsHippoRAGCatBWins$ of 100 queries against Flat, GraphRAG and HippoRAG, with $\TerraVsFlatRAGCatBTies$, $\TerraVsGraphRAGCatBTies$ and $\TerraVsHippoRAGCatBTies$ ties. \subsubsection{ROUGE-L Lexical Trade-off and Recall Disentanglement}
ROUGE-L F1 penalizes length through candidate-length precision ($\text{LCS}/|\text{cand}|$), and the reference holdings average $70.8$ words (computed against researcher-constructed references, \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json}, SHA256 \texttt{8144fa81...}, by deterministic tokenized LCS; F1 is the mean of per-query F1, not the harmonic mean of the macro P and R). On Category~B, Flat Vector RAG has the highest F1 ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougeFOne}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougeFOne$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougeFOne$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougeFOne$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougeFOne$) and precision ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougePrecision}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougePrecision$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougePrecision$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougePrecision$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougePrecision$), because TERRA writes longer chronological syntheses (mean words in Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance}). On recall, TERRA's firewall falsely refuses \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries (scored zero), giving $\TerraCatBRougeRecall$ against $\FlatRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (Flat), $\GraphRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (GraphRAG), $\HippoRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (HippoRAG) and $\mathbf{\DirectLLMCatBRougeRecall}$ (Direct LLM); on answered queries TERRA reaches \TerraCatBAnsweredRougeRecall\ (mean \TerraCatBAnsweredMeanWords\ words), comparable to Flat's \FlatRAGCatBAnsweredRougeRecall. N-gram overlap cannot separate valid modern doctrine from overruled precedent, since it rewards verbatim citation of dead law; TERRA's strengths lie in verified citation-graph recovery (Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}) and dual-judge faithfulness ($\TerraCatBFaithfulness$, FDR $q < 0.05$).

\subsection{Temporal Parametric Leakage Stress Test}
\label{subsec:temporal-leakage}

Models pretrained on post-$T$ legal history risk \textit{temporal parametric leakage}, anachronistically importing later doctrinal shifts or overrulings into analyses framed at cutoff $T$. We preregistered and ran a 50-query probe across five horizons ($T \in \{1890, 1930, 1950, 1970, 1980\}$), spanning seven doctrinal domains and balanced across case prominence and reasoning depth. Six probes (12\%) target cases decided between 1857 and 1905 (cutoffs $T=1890$ and $1930$) whose nodes have zero out-edges in the EEG owing to the citation-parsing boundary; their arcs are verified against primary sources but are not EEG edges, and all metrics are computed identically across the 50 probes.

\subsubsection{Design, Metrics and Evaluator Reliability}
The probe evaluates \TemporalTotalEvaluations\ responses from Direct LLM, Flat Vector RAG, $\text{TERRA}_{\text{ungated}}$ ($L_{\text{gen}}$) and $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ ($L_{\text{final}}$), each under \textbf{Condition A} (standard prompt) and \textbf{Condition B} (explicit instruction to adhere to year $T$), under a preregistered 3-tier rubric: Level~0 (clean), Level~1 (non-prejudicial mention or disclaimer) and Level~2 (fatal reliance on post-$T$ law). The primary metric is the \textbf{Substantive Post-$T$ Leakage Rate (SPTLR)}, the share of Level~2 failures. Because refusing systems generate no post-$T$ text and look ``leak-free'', we decouple containment from problem-solving with the \textbf{Refusal Rate} and the \textbf{Historical Legal Correctness Rate (HLCR)}, whether the system states the operative rule as of $T$, and we measure the \textbf{NLI Gate Leakage Interception Rate (NGLIR)}, the share of ungated leaking candidates intercepted by the gate (denominator $D$).

Responses were judged by \texttt{qwen3-next-80b} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}. Over $N=\TemporalValidPairs$ complete pairs the judges reached $\TemporalRawConcordance$ raw concordance and $100\%$ monotonic inclusion (every GPT-OSS leak was within Qwen's flags), but quadratic weighted Cohen's $\kappa$ on the three-level severity rating was $\TemporalQwk$, lower than elsewhere (e.g., $\kappa=\ObscKappa$ on the obscure suite) and consistent with the \textit{Kappa Paradox}~\cite{feinstein1990high}: GPT-OSS rated $91.7\%$ of responses Level~0 ($289/315$), inflating chance agreement to $\approx 60\%$. Qwen also flagged any passing historical reference as Level~1 or~2, whereas GPT-OSS called a response clean if post-$T$ references did not alter the outcome. Evaluations were reconciled by a pre-specified 5-tier protocol: (1)~safe refusals resolve to Level~0; (2)~unanimity is preserved; (3)~lexical breach of forbidden phrases and (4)~substantive quotation of post-$T$ law assign Level~2; (5)~subtle mentions resolve to $\max(s_1,s_2)=\text{Level~1}$. Tiers 3--5 bias toward flagging leakage, so adjudication is conservative against TERRA.

\subsubsection{Missingness and Sensitivity Bounds}
Of the $400$ evaluations, $85$ GPT-OSS calls ended in provider-side safety-filter terminations. Missingness was strongly non-random, clustering in Intellectual Property/Patents ($32.1\%$, $18/56$), Antitrust ($23.2\%$, $13/56$) and Commerce ($23.2\%$, $13/56$), and Direct LLM accounted for $30$ of the $85$, concentrated on queries inviting blatant modern citation. Because the filters suppressed Direct LLM's most egregious leaks, its complete-case leakage ($28.0\%$ in Condition A) is an underestimate. We therefore report sensitivity bounds $[SPTLR_{\text{lower}}, SPTLR_{\text{upper}}]$ over all $2^{85}$ missing-data assignments and complete discordant-pair counts $(b,c)$: $b$ counts pairs where $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ is clean (Level~0 or~1) while the baseline shows Level~2 leakage, $c$ the reverse, each for complete cases ($N_{\text{cc}}$, both judges finished) and for the full $N=50$ bounds.

\textbf{Headline rates.} Under Condition A, SPTLR bounds are \DirectLlmSptlrA\ for Direct LLM, \FlatRagSptlrA\ for Flat RAG, \TerraUngatedSptlrA\ for $\text{TERRA}_{\text{ungated}}$ and \TerraGatedSptlrA\ for $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ (refusal rates \DirectLlmRefusalA, \FlatRagRefusalA, \TerraUngatedRefusalA\ and \TerraGatedRefusalA; HLCR \DirectLlmHlcrA, \FlatRagHlcrA, \TerraUngatedHlcrA\ and \TerraGatedHlcrA). Under Condition B, the SPTLR bounds are \DirectLlmSptlrB, \FlatRagSptlrB, \TerraUngatedSptlrB\ and \TerraGatedSptlrB\ in the same order (refusal \DirectLlmRefusalB, \FlatRagRefusalB, \TerraUngatedRefusalB, \TerraGatedRefusalB; HLCR \DirectLlmHlcrB, \FlatRagHlcrB, \TerraUngatedHlcrB, \TerraGatedHlcrB). The gate interception rate (NGLIR) is $[0.0\%, 20.0\%]$ under Condition A and \NglirRange\ under Condition B, on very small denominators ($D=\NglirDenominatorQwen$ leaking candidates under Qwen, \NglirQwen\ intercepted; $D=\NglirDenominatorConsensus$ under consensus, \NglirConsensus); a stratified spot-check of \CleanSpotCheckEvaluations\ Level-0 records found \CleanSpotCheckFalseNegatives\ false negatives (one-sided upper bound \CleanSpotCheckUpperOneSided).

\subsubsection{Primary Hypothesis $H_1$: Metric Decoupling and Refusal Masking}
Preregistered $H_1$ predicted lower raw SPTLR for $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ than Flat Vector RAG under Condition A. It is \textbf{not supported}: complete cases ($N_{\text{cc}}=36$) give $b=0, c=3$ (one-sided exact McNemar $p=\HoneSptlrPval$; two-sided $p=0.2500$, or $0.0625$ if missing records are zero-imputed at $N=50$), the bounds are $b \in [0,5], c \in [7,8]$, and Flat RAG's raw leakage ($\FlatRagSptlrA$) is lower than TERRA's ($\TerraGatedSptlrA$). The discordant pairs show why: Flat RAG produced no leaks where TERRA was clean ($b=0$) because it refused $\FlatRagRefusalA$ of queries ($23/50$), and a system that refuses cannot leak, whereas TERRA engaged (refusal rate $\TerraGatedRefusalA$) and incurred $c=3$ complete-case Level-2 classifications on complex multi-jurisdictional tests. On HLCR, $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ reaches $\mathbf{\TerraGatedHlcrA}$ correctness against $\FlatRagHlcrA$ for Flat RAG ($b=20, c=1$; exact McNemar $p=\HoneHlcrPvalFormatted$, $p<0.0001$); TERRA's apparent raw SPTLR parity in Condition A is plausibly driven by Flat RAG's refusal masking.

\subsubsection{Hypotheses $H_2$--$H_6$, Directional Stability and Gate Attribution}
For $H_2$ (TERRA vs.\ Direct LLM, Condition A), complete cases ($N_{\text{cc}}=32$) give $b=2, c=4$; bounding over the 18 missing Direct LLM evaluations gives $b \in [11,16]$, $c \in [5,6]$ ($p \in [\HtwoPvalMin, \HtwoPvalMax]$). Since $c_{\max}=6<b_{\min}=11$, the sign is stable (\textbf{Directional Stability}) under all $2^{85}$ assignments, although the complete cases favour Direct LLM and $p=\HtwoPvalMin$ holds only at the most favourable bound. For $H_3$ (vs.\ Flat RAG, Condition B), $N_{\text{cc}}=29$ gives $b=5, c=1$; Flat RAG's refusal rate falls to $30.0\%$ under explicit prompting, exposing leakage ($\FlatRagSptlrB$); bounds are $b \in [10,13]$, $c \in [4,8]$ ($p \in [\HthreePvalMin, \HthreePvalMax]$), directionally stable ($c_{\max}=8<b_{\min}=10$). For $H_4$ (vs.\ Direct LLM, Condition B), $N_{\text{cc}}=31$ gives $b=1, c=1$; even when instructed, Direct LLM leaks ($\DirectLlmSptlrB$); bounds are $b \in [8,11]$, $c \in [2,6]$ ($p \in [\HfourPvalMin, \HfourPvalMax]$), directionally stable ($c_{\max}=6<b_{\min}=8$). The gate-ablation tests $H_5, H_6$ are underpowered at $N=50$ ($b \in [0,2], c \in [1,1]$ in Condition A; $b \in [2,5], c \in [0,4]$ in Condition B; complete cases $b=0, c=1$ and $b=2, c=0$). Rather than a high-volume statistical filter, the NLI gate acted as a \textbf{targeted qualitative safety firewall}, making six interventions: it intercepted one Level-2 leak in Condition B (\textit{United States v. Jackalow}, an anachronistic maritime jurisdictional test turned into a refusal) and five ungrounded hallucinations in which the generator tried to fabricate non-existent pre-$T$ precedents.

\subsection{External Benchmark Generalization and Anti-Circularity Audit (CaseFacts)}
\label{subsec:casefacts-generalization}

Evaluating only on researcher-constructed queries risks circular alignment or benchmark overfitting, so we also evaluate on \textbf{CaseFacts} \cite{putta2026casefactsbenchmarklegalfactchecking}, a legal fact-checking dataset built from U.S. Supreme Court decisions by an external team.

\subsubsection{Anti-Circularity and Graph Substrate Audit}
Of the $20{,}000$ nodes, exactly $34$ landmark decisions ($\CaseFactsSeedDensity$, $\CaseFactsSeedDensityRaw$) received curated reasoning traces during early development (not in the evaluated index), whereas the 350-query benchmark touches $284$ distinct nodes ($\CaseFactsFootprintDensity$, $\CaseFactsFootprintNodes$; 100 in Category~A, 151 in B, 0 in C, 58 in D, with 25 nodes of multi-category overlap), leaving $\mathbf{\CaseFactsUntouchedSubstrate}$ of the substrate ($\CaseFactsUntouchedNodes$ nodes) unvisited. The 19 Category-D queries map to 9 distinct edges among the 56 tagged overrulings (list from CRS R45319 via a Wikipedia mirror; 53 audited as consistent, 3 mis-resolved and unused by Category~D); this shows they are recognised overrulings, not unfitted selection. Category~B chains span 3 to 5 nodes (2 to 4 hops): \CatBQueriesLenThree\ have 3 nodes, \CatBQueriesLenFour\ have 4 and \CatBQueriesLenFive\ have 5, and Full TERRA's full-path recovery falls with chain length (\CatBTerraPathRecallLenThree, \CatBTerraPathRecallLenFour\ and \CatBTerraPathRecallLenFive), so performance is not invariant across lengths.

\subsubsection{Empirical Findings}
\textbf{Track~1 (Table~\ref{tab:casefacts_eval}, Panel~A) is mixed.} Full TERRA's three-class Macro-$F_1$ is $\CaseFactsTerraMacroFOne$, above Flat Vector RAG ($\CaseFactsFlatMacroFOne$; $\CaseFactsTerraLiftFlat$) and Direct LLM ($\CaseFactsDirectMacroFOne$; $\CaseFactsTerraLiftDirect$), but the gain comes entirely from the Overruled class ($n=8$): over Supported and Refuted alone the macro is $\CaseFactsTerraMacroSR$ for TERRA against $\CaseFactsFlatMacroSR$ for Flat and $\CaseFactsDirectMacroSR$ for Direct, TERRA's Supported $F_1$ is the lowest of the three, and its Refuted $F_1$ is below Flat's. Accuracy, counting out-of-corpus predictions as errors, is lowest for TERRA ($\CaseFactsTerraAccCount$ against $\CaseFactsBaselineAccCount$ for each baseline); the NLI gate converted 25 borderline in-corpus queries into out-of-corpus refusals when retrieved context was legally incomplete. As a diagnostic with exact Clopper-Pearson 95\% intervals, TERRA identifies $\mathbf{\CaseFactsTerraOverruled}$ Overruled cases (95\% CI: $\CaseFactsTerraOverruledCI$), double Flat Vector RAG ($\CaseFactsFlatOverruled$, $\CaseFactsFlatOverruledCI$) and Direct LLM ($\CaseFactsDirectOverruled$, $\CaseFactsDirectOverruledCI$); the intervals overlap, so the difference is not significant. Of the 8 pairs, 2 (\textit{Wolf $\to$ Mapp}, \textit{Olmstead $\to$ Katz}) have direct \texttt{OVERRULES} edges in the EEG and 6 rest on in-graph citation paths. None of the 4 non-recalled cases involved fabrication: 2 were intercepted by the gate (\textit{Plessy}, \textit{Schenck}), 1 was a defensible label discordance (\textit{Cicenia v. Lagay}), and 1 was a retrieval-depth limit (\textit{Chimel v. California}, whose overruling authority \textit{United States v. Robinson} lay beyond the 2-hop boundary; Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}).

\textbf{Track~2 (Panel~B) shows full out-of-corpus discrimination.} TERRA classifies $\mathbf{\CaseFactsTerraRefusalTrackTwo}$ ($100.0\%$) of modern cases as out-of-corpus, against Flat Vector RAG ($\CaseFactsFlatRefusalTrackTwo$, $92.0\%$) and Direct LLM ($\CaseFactsDirectRefusalTrackTwo$, $80.0\%$). Of the 50 queries, $\CaseFactsTerraHardRefusalTrackTwo$ ($92.0\%$) were short-circuited by the NLI gate and $\CaseFactsTerraDisclosedTrackTwo$ ($8.0\%$) were disclosed pre-1980 analyses ending in \texttt{OUTSIDE PRECEDENT CORPUS}. Examination of all 50 completions found $\CaseFactsTerraHallucinationTrackTwo$ ($0.0\%$) hallucination and no phantom citations, whereas Direct LLM hallucinated substantive answers on $\CaseFactsDirectHallucinationTrackTwo$ ($20.0\%$) and Flat RAG on $\CaseFactsFlatHallucinationTrackTwo$ ($8.0\%$).

\subsection{Standardized External Benchmark Evaluation on CLERC (NAACL 2025)}
\label{subsec:clerc-generalization}

To test whether the architecture generalizes beyond researcher-crafted queries, we evaluate TERRA on a stratified sample of \textbf{CLERC} (Findings of NAACL 2025) \cite{hou2024clerc}, a legal retrieval and drafting benchmark built by Johns Hopkins University and collaborators. Our validation thus has four layers: the internal controlled benchmark ($N=\numUniqueQueries$; Sections~\ref{subsec:safety-and-factual}--\ref{subsec:ablation-study}), CLERC (this section), CaseFacts (Section~\ref{subsec:casefacts-generalization}), and licensed-practitioner evaluation, which is not done (Limitation~1, Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}).

\subsubsection{Empirical Findings}
\textbf{Track~1 (Table~\ref{tab:clerc_eval}, Panel~A) is mixed.} In retrieval (Task~1A), Full TERRA has slightly higher Recall@10 ($\ClercTerraRecallTen$ vs.\ $\ClercFlatRecallTen$) and nDCG@10 ($\ClercTerraNDCG$ vs.\ $\ClercFlatNDCG$) than Flat Vector RAG, a one-query difference in hits@10 ($\ClercTerraHitsTen$ vs.\ $\ClercFlatHitsTen$; MRR@10 $\ClercTerraMRR$ vs.\ $\ClercFlatMRR$), so the margin is modest ($\ClercTerraRecallTenDelta$ points). In drafting (Task~1B), TERRA attains $\ClercTerraRougeL$ ROUGE-L and $\ClercTerraBleu$ BLEU-4 and the highest Citation Precision ($\text{CP}=\ClercTerraCitePrecision$ vs.\ $\ClercFlatCitePrecision$ for Flat and $\ClercDirectCitePrecision$ for Direct), with Citation Recall $\ClercTerraCiteRecall$ (Flat $\ClercFlatCiteRecall$, Direct $\ClercDirectCiteRecall$) and Citation $F_1$ $\ClercTerraCiteFOne$. Direct LLM has the highest Citation $F_1$ ($4.7\%$, against TERRA's $3.5\%$ and Flat's $1.8\%$; micro-pooled over items; TERRA's pooled precision omits its 53 gate-refused items, which carry no citations, while its recall still counts them), and TERRA's judged soundness is the lowest of the three ($\ClercTerraSoundness$ against $\ClercFlatSoundness$ and $\ClercDirectSoundness$).

We recomputed a citation audit from the raw Track~1 completions. Among case captions extracted by pattern from judge-flagged completions, the share matching no corpus title is $\ClercTerraExternalCitePct$ for TERRA (43/281), $15.0\%$ for Flat (88/585) and $\ClercDirectFabricationTrackOne$ for Direct LLM (147/358); the remaining TERRA captions resolve to in-corpus decisions ($\ClercTerraInCorpusCitePct$), and gate-intercepted TERRA completions carry no citations ($0/53$). This is a corpus-membership check, not an existence check: the unmatched captions include real Supreme Court decisions outside the 20k subset as well as extraction fragments, so we do not report a fabrication rate, and an earlier recorded value of $0.0\%$ fabrication for TERRA and Flat, which this recomputation does not reproduce, is withdrawn. Dual judging nevertheless flagged doctrinal misapplication in $\ClercTerraMisapplicationTrackOne$ of all 120 completions ($\ClercTerraMisapplicationOrTrackOne$ under OR, $\ClercTerraMisapplicationAndTrackOne$ under AND; Flat $\ClercFlatMisapplicationTrackOne$, Direct $\ClercDirectMisapplicationTrackOne$, neither gated). All of TERRA's flags fall among the 67 completions generated on incomplete retrieval subgraphs ($\ClercTerraMisappGenOr$ OR, $\ClercTerraMisappGenAnd$ AND), where the generator reasoned by analogy because the controlling precedent lay beyond the 2-hop radius: authentic evidence does not equate to sufficient evidence, which motivates the path-recovery analysis in Section~\ref{subsec:retrieval-quality}.

\textbf{Track~2 (Panel~B) shows strong refusal.} TERRA refuses $\mathbf{\ClercTerraRefusalTrackTwo}$ of the out-of-corpus queries (Flat $\ClercFlatRefusalTrackTwo$, Direct $\ClercDirectRefusalTrackTwo$; $3.3\times$ the baselines), of which the NLI gate intercepted $\ClercTerraHardRefusalTrackTwo$ before generation; none of the 86 gate-triggering events across both tracks (0/53, 0/33) contained a fabricated citation. Track~2 is an engineered boundary test, not a task-utility metric. The same corpus-membership check leaves $8.7\%$ of TERRA's Track~2 captions unmatched (6/69; Flat $11.5\%$, Direct LLM $\ClercDirectFabricationTrackTwo$), and on the 17 completions generated without gate short-circuit ($\ClercTerraMisapplicationOrTrackTwo$ of all 50; 100.0\% of generated completions) both judges flagged doctrinal misapplication ($\ClercTerraMisapplicationTrackTwo$), as the model answered post-1980 or statutory questions with pre-1980 authorities.

\subsection{Direct Evidence Retrieval Quality and Precedent-Chain Coverage}
\label{subsec:retrieval-quality}

Do downstream generative results reflect better evidence retrieval, or only the generator's ability to synthesize plausible analyses? Because TERRA's expansion uses breadth $k=2$ and depth $d=2$ while Category~B arcs span 3 to 5 nodes (2 to 4 hops), we evaluate retrieval as a function of chain length. To avoid conflating single-point lookups (routed through the parametric Fast Path) or unanswerable probes, we score raw evidence retrieval on the $N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ Category~B trajectories ($\CatBGoldPrecedents$ gold landmark precedents) before generation. The four systems return heterogeneous representations (ranked chunks, unranked community reports, unranked PPR clusters, and a 2-hop directed EEG subgraph), so ranked-list metrics such as MRR or nDCG cannot be applied uniformly; we report deterministic dual-resolution entity recall (CAP Node ID and canonical title) and full-trajectory recovery in Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}, computed on the stored \texttt{context\_full} fields of the canonical v2 file (SHA256 prefix \texttt{95e775e2}) that the generator actually received.

\subsubsection{Precedent-Chain Recovery and Chain-Length Disaggregation}
Flat Vector RAG reaches $\CatBFlatMacroNodeRecall$ macro node recall ($\CatBFlatMicroNodeRecall$ micro) and recovers the complete trajectory for only $\CatBFlatFullPathRecall$ of queries ($\CatBFlatFullPathCount$): dense embeddings find one or two lexically adjacent landmarks but miss intermediate stepping-stones. GraphRAG-Adapted reaches $\CatBGraphRAGMacroNodeRecall$ node recall and $\CatBGraphRAGFullPathRecall$ full-path recovery ($\CatBGraphRAGFullPathCount$), since static Louvain communities group cases topically without chronology. HippoRAG-Adapted has substantially higher node recall ($\CatBHippoRAGMacroNodeRecall$) but only $\CatBHippoRAGFullPathRecall$ full-path recall ($\CatBHippoRAGFullPathCount$), as undirected Personalized PageRank spreads mass over high-degree peripheral precedents. Full TERRA reaches $\CatBTerraMacroNodeRecall$ macro node recall ($\CatBTerraMicroNodeRecall$ micro) and recovers the full chain on $\CatBTerraFullPathCount$/100 queries, a $\CatBTerraVsFlatNodeRecallDelta$ node-recall lift and $\CatBTerraVsFlatPathRecallFactor$ path-recovery factor over Flat Vector RAG ($\CatBFlatFullPathCount$/100), and $\CatBTerraVsHippoNodeRecallDelta$ and $\CatBTerraVsHippoPathRecallFactor$ over HippoRAG.

By chain length (Panel~B): on the $N=\CatBQueriesLenThree$ 3-node chains (2 hops), full-path recovery is $\CatBFlatPathRecallLenThree$ for Flat ($\CatBFlatPathCountLenThree$), $\CatBGraphRAGPathRecallLenThree$ for GraphRAG ($\CatBGraphRAGPathCountLenThree$), $\CatBHippoRAGPathRecallLenThree$ for HippoRAG ($\CatBHippoRAGPathCountLenThree$) and $\CatBTerraPathRecallLenThree$ for TERRA ($\CatBTerraPathCountLenThree$; node recall $\CatBTerraNodeRecallLenThree$). On the $N=\CatBQueriesLenFour$ 4-node chains (3 hops), Flat ($\CatBFlatPathRecallLenFour$) and GraphRAG ($\CatBGraphRAGPathRecallLenFour$) recover none and HippoRAG $\CatBHippoRAGPathRecallLenFour$ ($\CatBHippoRAGPathCountLenFour$), against TERRA's $\CatBTerraPathRecallLenFour$ ($\CatBTerraPathCountLenFour$; node recall $\CatBTerraNodeRecallLenFour$). On the $N=\CatBQueriesLenFive$ 5-node chains (4 hops), all baselines recover $0/5$ and TERRA $\CatBTerraPathRecallLenFive$ ($\CatBTerraPathCountLenFive$; node recall $\CatBTerraNodeRecallLenFive$; exact 95\% CI \CatBFiveNodeClopperPearsonCI), a stratum too small for more than a descriptive diagnostic.

\subsubsection{Multi-Seed Anchoring}
For an evolutionary query $q$, entity and legal-concept extraction yields seeds $S_q \subset V$ with $|S_q| \ge 2$ (mean $\CatBMeanSeedsPerQuery$ per Category~B query; $\CatBTwoSeedsPct$ with two, $\CatBThreeSeedsPct$ with three, $\CatBFourPlusSeedsPct$ with four or more), and each seed expands a $d=2$ ball along forward and backward citation edges with breadth $k=2$. Multi-seed extraction is designed to anchor both extremities of a trajectory (index 0 and $m-1$); seed placement was not re-audited for the canonical run, so this is a mechanism explanation, not a measured result. For a chain $v_0 \to \dots \to v_{m-1}$, the forward ball $B(v_0,2)$ covers $\{v_0,v_1,v_2\}$ and the reverse ball $B(v_{m-1},2)$ covers $\{v_{m-1},v_{m-2},v_{m-3}\}$, so when branching stays within the beam the two neighborhoods meet at intermediate authorities and can cover paths of up to four hops without deeper search. In the canonical run all gold nodes were recovered for $\CatBTerraPathCountLenFour$ 4-node and $\CatBTerraPathCountLenFive$ 5-node chains; high fan-out exceeding the beam is a plausible but untested explanation for the 16 incompletely recovered 4-node chains. We did not test causally whether TERRA's results (Tables~\ref{tab:overall_summary} and~\ref{tab:clerc_eval}) stem from retrieval quality; Direct LLM's higher Category~B faithfulness shows retrieval alone does not explain faithfulness.

\label{subsec:citation-correctness}

Legal validity depends on whether the generator cites and attributes doctrine correctly in its final completions, since language models commonly invent case names, cite authorities for propositions they never established, or hallucinate citations on unanswerable inquiries. Table~ef{tab:citation_eval} therefore evaluates citation fidelity in the synthesized completions across the 
umUniqueQueries-query suite (
umTotalEvals\ evaluations over 
umComparativePipelines\ pipelines). TERRA's entity citation precision is \TerraEntityCitePrecision\ (earlier single-judge run \TerraEntityCitePrecisionLegacy), and \CitationLinksResolved\ of \CitationLinksEmitted\ emitted links resolved (\CitationLinkResolutionRate).

On Category~B ($N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ queries, $\CatBGoldPrecedents$ gold authorities; Table~\ref{tab:citation_eval}, Panel~A), Full TERRA has the highest macro citation recall, $\mathbf{\CatBTerraMacroCitationRecall}$ ($\CatBTerraMicroCitationRecall$ micro), ahead of HippoRAG-Adapted ($\CatBHippoRAGMacroCitationRecall$), Direct LLM ($\CatBDirectMacroCitationRecall$), Flat Vector RAG ($\CatBFlatMacroCitationRecall$) and GraphRAG-Adapted ($\CatBGraphRAGMacroCitationRecall$) by $\CatBTerraVsHippoCitationRecallDelta$ to $\CatBTerraVsGraphCitationRecallDelta$ points. Across the suite (Panel~B), TERRA emitted $\mathbf{\TerraTotalMarkdownLinks}$ interactive links (Section~\ref{subsubsec:xai-provenance}); $\mathbf{\TerraResolvedMarkdownLinks/\TerraTotalMarkdownLinks}$ ($\mathbf{\TerraMarkdownLinkResolutionRate}$) pass the project's validator, which accepts a link when its identifier exists in the index or its caption matches an indexed title or alias, with $\mathbf{\TerraMarkdownLinkFidelityRate}$ title-to-node fidelity (including aliases such as the \textit{Slaughter-House Cases} resolving to \textit{Butchers' Benevolent Ass'n}, \texttt{83\_0036-01}). \subsection{Computational Budget Profiling and Geometric Gate Calibration}
\label{subsec:computational-budget}

Multi-stage pipelines compound latency, tokens and cost, so Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget} profiles operations per query, active 70B generator calls, stage and end-to-end latency, token volumes and modelled cost for all \numComparativePipelines\ architectures, together with a calibration of the Tier~2 geometric pre-filter on the 20,000-case index.

\subsubsection{Sequential Pipeline Operations and Call Parity}
The single-shot baselines run a two-stage retrieve-then-generate pipeline ($\FlatRAGTotalOpsPerQuery$ operations per query) with $\FlatRAGGenCallsFormatted$ generator calls over the $N=\numUniqueQueries$ queries. TERRA runs $q \rightarrow$ Router $\rightarrow$ Tier~2 Gate $\rightarrow$ EEG BFS $\rightarrow$ NLI Grader $\rightarrow$ 70B Generator and performs \TerraOperationsTotalCount\ operations (\TerraOperationsPerQuery\ per query; counted where a stage recorded non-zero time) at a modelled \TerraDeployedCostPerThousand\ per 1,000 queries (Gemma~3 12B router; Llama~3.3 70B grader and generator). The cost is modelled from token estimates at list prices, not metered; it prices a grader call for every Category~B--D query (twice for refused Category~C and~D queries) and none for Category~A, although Category~A recorded grading time. Pricing one grader call only where recorded grading time was at least 1~ms gives \$4.66 per 1,000 queries.

The counts come from recorded stage times. Category~A (the nominal fast path) recorded retrieval and grading time on all 100 queries and invoked the generator on \TerraCatAGenCallsFormatted; Category~B recorded all four stages and generated on \TerraCatBGenCallsFormatted; Category~C recorded routing, retrieval and grading on all 75 queries but never generated (all refused; for 74 the grading time was under 1~ms and the context empty, consistent with a deterministic empty-context rejection, not an LLM grading call); Category~D recorded all three pre-generation stages and generated on \TerraCatDGenCallsFormatted, the other 46 being refused before generation (7 with an empty context), and the generated textual refusals D068 and D070 bring explicit refusals to 48. This gives \TerraCatATotalOps, \TerraCatBTotalOps, \TerraCatCTotalOps\ and \TerraCatDTotalOps\ operations on Categories~A--D (\TerraCatATotalOpsPerQuery, \TerraCatBTotalOpsPerQuery, \TerraCatCTotalOpsPerQuery\ and \TerraCatDTotalOpsPerQuery\ per query) and \TerraBenchmarkTotalOpsFormatted\ in total (\TerraOverallTotalOpsPerQuery\ per query). Every Category~C query recorded retrieval time (at least 178~ms excluding routing), so no query was terminated before retrieval and the threshold analysis in Panel~B calibrates a candidate pre-filter rather than describing the deployed run.

TERRA invokes the generator on only \TerraOverallGenCallsCount\ of 350 queries (\TerraOverallGenCallsPct), a \TerraOverallGenCallsReductionPct\ reduction against the baselines' $350/350$, but the reduction comes from refusals (Category~C made none, Category~D \TerraCatDGenCallsFormatted, and some Category~A and~B refusals also skip generation) and is not a reduction in 70B use: the Llama~3.3 70B grader recorded at least 1~ms on 276 of 350 queries, so generator and grader calls together exceed the baselines' one call per query.

\subsubsection{Latency and Cost Trade-Offs}
On Category~B, TERRA has a median latency of $\TerraHardPathMedianSeconds\text{ s}$ ($\TerraCatBLatencyMeanMS\text{ ms}$ mean) and a modelled cost of $\TerraCatBTotalCostPerThousand$ per 1,000 queries ($\TerraCatBPerQueryCost$ per query), against $\FlatRAGLatencyMedMS\text{ ms}$ and $\FlatRAGTotalCostPerThousand$ per 1,000 ($\FlatRAGPerQueryCost$ per query) for Flat Vector RAG, a $\TerraCatBVsFlatCostRatio$ per-query cost ratio. We disclose this overhead as deliberate: Flat Vector RAG recovers the full precedent path on only $\CatBFlatFullPathRecall$ of queries ($\CatBFlatFullPathCount$) against TERRA's $\CatBTerraFullPathRecall$ ($\CatBTerraFullPathCount$; Section~\ref{subsec:retrieval-quality}), and where missing stepping-stones carry malpractice risk we judge about $\TerraHardPathMedianSeconds\text{ s}$ and $\TerraCatBPerQueryCost$ per query (modelled) a defensible price for that recovery.

\subsubsection{Stage Latency Profiling}
Panel~A reports mean stage times from logged timing fields. For hard-route queries (Categories~B--D, 240 of 350) the logged retrieval timer is cumulative and includes routing (correlation $r=0.999$; difference at least 178~ms), so retrieval is logged retrieval minus routing; for fast-route queries the timers are separate. Stages sum exactly to end-to-end time for Category~A and the single-shot baselines, but for Categories~B--D they leave an unattributed remainder of unestablished cause (mean $\TerraCatBRemainderMS\text{ ms}$, $\TerraCatCRemainderMS\text{ ms}$ and $\TerraCatDRemainderMS\text{ ms}$), so the columns do not reconcile exactly. Routing averages $\TerraOverallDecoupledRoutingMS\text{ ms}$ ($\TerraCatADecoupledRoutingMS\text{ ms}$ on A, $\TerraCatBDecoupledRoutingMS\text{ ms}$ on B). Retrieval averages $\TerraOverallDecoupledRetrievalMS\text{ ms}$ ($\TerraCatADecoupledRetrievalMS$, $\TerraCatBDecoupledRetrievalMS$, $\TerraCatCDecoupledRetrievalMS$ and $\TerraCatDDecoupledRetrievalMS\text{ ms}$ on A--D); the Category~A fast path does not bypass retrieval. To test traversal stability under corpus growth without generative confounding, we run standalone breadth-first traversal over four snapshot expansions: $1890\to1930$ (Step $N=40$~yr), $1930\to1950$ (20~yr), $1950\to1970$ (20~yr) and $1970\to1980$ (10~yr). Grand pooled recall moved from $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTMeanStd$ to $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTNMeanStd$ ($\Delta\text{Recall}=\IssueNineteenOverallDeltaRecallMeanStd$), with $\IssueNineteenStabilityCoefficient$ of queries showing $\Delta\text{Recall} \ge 0$, a Discovery Rate on newly eligible authorities of $\IssueNineteenDiscoveryRateMean$, and median traversal latency under one millisecond (\IssueNineteenBFSLatencyMedianMs~ms; mean $0.15 \pm 0.18$~ms); by snapshot pair, $\Delta\text{Recall}$ is $\IssueNineteenPairIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1890\to1930$), $\IssueNineteenPairIIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1930\to1950$), $\IssueNineteenPairIIIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1950\to1970$) and $\IssueNineteenPairIVDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1970\to1980$), and the full per-snapshot table is in the supplementary material. Three boundaries apply: absolute recall includes the depth-0 seed (while $\Delta\text{Recall}$ is invariant to that offset); negative shifts stem from degree caps when expanding nodes become hubs; and the experiment evaluates topology over generic \texttt{CITES} edges on NetworkX DiGraphs, decoupled from vector retrieval (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}) and from live index upsert, which remains future work.

The evaluation indicates where TERRA helps (Category~B retrieval coverage, out-of-domain refusal) and where it does not (Category~B faithfulness against Direct LLM, obscure precedents without curated labels).

\subsection{Empirical Analysis of Firewall Component Contributions and Scale Dynamics}
\label{subsec:firewall-analysis}

The design intended the Domain Boundary Firewall as a pre-retrieval filter in which vector distance ($d_{L2} < 1.3$) flags out-of-domain (OOD) queries. A preliminary 50-query Category C audit on the initial 10,009-opinion index found the gate non-functional at that scale ($0/50$ intercepted), since OOD distances ($0.281 \le d_{L2} \le 0.859$) fell entirely below $1.3$. Safety in Table~\ref{tab:overall_summary} (\TerraCatCRejectionRate\ refusal on Category C; \TerraCatDRejectionRate\ refusal and $\TerraCatDRefutationRate$\ verified refutation on Category D) was therefore delivered by downstream refusal rather than by the proximity gate. In the canonical run, 81 of the 139 refusals occurred on an empty retrieved context (74 in Category~C, 7 in Category~D) and 58 on a non-empty one (2, 16, 1 and 39 in Categories~A--D). In the 35-query pilot ablation (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}, Ablation 2), removing NLI reduced adversarial safety (scored as refusal) to 0.0\% on five Category~D queries, so the grader was necessary there; the ablation does not apportion the Category~C refusals between empty-context and entailment-based refusal.

On the 20,000-opinion corpus (Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget}, Panel~B), the full $N=75$ Category~C suite gives an isolated AUROC of $\TerraGateIsolatedAUROC$. At $\tau = 1.30$, offline calibration gives $\TerraGateFPRTauOneThreeZero$ in-domain false refusal ($\TerraGateFPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) and flags $\TerraGateTPRTauOneThreeZero$ ($\TerraGateTPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) of the OOD probes by distance; the deployed run terminated no query before retrieval. That 50/50 probes fell below $1.3$ on the 10k index while 41/75 exceed it on the 20k index is consistent with density effects as the corpus grows across seven constitutional domains, but two snapshots do not support a scaling law. We therefore treat geometric proximity only as an optional coarse pre-filter that could save compute on obvious outliers.

This paper introduced TERRA, an experimental dual-phase GraphRAG architecture addressing knowledge drift and multi-step legal reasoning on historical SCOTUS jurisprudence (\CorpusTemporalSpan). Structuring \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic decisions (\CorpusPrecedentEdges\ citation edges) with procedural reasoning traces, TERRA enables inference via Traffic Cop routing, BFS traversal, and an NLI grader evaluating retrieved evidence. Benchmarking across \numUniqueQueries\ queries (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations) shows higher Category~B multi-hop faithfulness than Flat Vector RAG, HippoRAG, and GraphRAG ($\Delta$ from $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ to $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$; $q<0.05$; the paired interval against Flat includes zero), though not over Direct LLM ($\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$); higher overall faithfulness ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$, overlapping CIs; $\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$); and $\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate$ adversarial safe handling ($\TerraCatDRejection$ refusals, \TerraCatDRefutations\ refutations). Constraints include \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors, false refusals on \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries, and reliance on curated overruling annotations (Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization}). Critically, because evaluations rely on automated LLM judges without licensed attorneys (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}), human expert review remains an essential prerequisite for deployment. In a standalone traversal test over four snapshot expansions, pooled recall shifted by $\IssueNineteenOverallDeltaRecallMeanStd$ (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}).
