The empirical evaluation validates that TERRA addresses fundamental failure modes of standard RAG architectures in knowledge-intensive, dynamic environments. This section contextualizes our primary architectural contributions, candidly examines current system limitations, and outlines future research directions.

\subsection{Empirical Analysis of Firewall Component Contributions and Scale Dynamics}
\label{subsec:firewall-analysis}

A critical finding from our systematic post-hoc auditing concerns the empirical division of labor within TERRA's safety architecture. The original design conceptualized the Domain Boundary Firewall as an active two-stage pre-retrieval filter where vector distance ($d_{L2} < 1.3$) flags out-of-domain (OOD) queries before graph traversal. However, systematic auditing across the preliminary 50-query Category C audit set on the initial 10,009-opinion index revealed that the vector proximity gate was non-functional at this scale ($0/50$ intercepted) because unconstrained OOD distances ($0.281 \le d_{L2} \le 0.859$) fell entirely beneath $1.3$.

Consequently, safety performance in Table~\ref{tab:overall_summary} (\TerraCatCRejectionRate\ refusal on Category C, \TerraCatDRejectionRate\ refusal and $\TerraCatDRefutationRate$\ verified refutation on Category D) was delivered almost entirely by the downstream NLI Smart Grader (Tier 3) via double-failure refusal. When OOD queries entered retrieval, the resulting lack of semantic entailment triggered a safe refusal. Removing NLI in ablation (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}, Ablation 2) caused an immediate collapse of adversarial safety to 0.0\%, confirming NLI as the true empirical safeguard.

Crucially, empirical calibration on the expanded 20,000-opinion substantive corpus demonstrates that geometric pre-filtering exhibits scale- and density-dependent behavior. As reported in Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget} (Panel~B), evaluating the full $N=75$ Category~C benchmark suite against the 20k index yields an isolated AUROC of $\TerraGateIsolatedAUROC$. At the operational threshold $\tau = 1.30$, geometric pre-filtering achieves $\TerraGateFPRTauOneThreeZero$ in-domain false refusal ($\TerraGateFPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) while intercepting $\TerraGateTPRTauOneThreeZero$ ($\TerraGateTPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) of out-of-domain probes pre-retrieval. Comparing the 10k index (where 50/50 probes fell below $1.3$) to the 20k index (where 41/75 probes exceed $1.3$) reflects an empirical observation of corpus manifold density: expanding corpus volume across seven verified constitutional domains creates denser semantic clustering, pushing extraneous out-of-domain queries farther into the embedding margin. We do not assert any generalized theoretical scaling law from these two empirical corpus snapshots; rather, we treat geometric proximity strictly as an optional coarse pre-filter that saves retrieval and NLI compute on obvious outliers, while downstream NLI entailment verification serves as the indispensable primary safety firewall.

To ensure complete scientific transparency and maintain the highest standard of academic integrity, we identify eighteen methodological limitations of the current architecture:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Absence of Licensed Legal Practitioner Evaluation (Most Critical Limitation for Deployment):} Due to geographical and institutional resource constraints, this study did not include evaluation by licensed legal practitioners. All faithfulness and safety assessments rely on automated LLM-as-a-judge scoring (Section~\ref{subsec:eval-metrics}) and continuous lexical metrics (ROUGE-L) evaluated against researcher-constructed reference answers cross-referenced against public legal reference sources (Cornell LII, Oyez, CRS Constitution Annotated). While the adversarial critic persona exhibits a modest, statistically significant correlation with reference lexical grounding (Pearson $r = \JudgePearsonR, p = \JudgePearsonP$), automated scoring cannot replicate practitioner judgment on subtle constitutional doctrine. Specifically, practitioners would assess legal correctness, temporal consistency, citation validity, and hallucination behavior beyond continuous metrics. Furthermore, lacking an independent labeled validation set for the NLI Smart Grader (Section~\ref{subsubsec:terra-nli-grader}), the false-non-entailment rate remains empirically unquantified beyond ablation evidence. We consider human expert evaluation of both legal output quality and NLI verifier reliability essential prerequisites for production deployment, and release the complete 350-query benchmark suite and codebase to invite independent expert replication. The author spot-check described in Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization} is a single non-expert review of a stratified sample and does not substitute for licensed practitioner review.
    \item \textbf{Metric Disentanglement and Refusal-Volume Masking:} Evaluating complex RAG pipelines solely via aggregate faithfulness induces severe metric distortion: systems with high epistemic refusal volume receive top marks for non-committal answers on unanswerable queries, masking generative weaknesses. Under our dual-judge protocol, TERRA has the highest overall ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$; intervals overlap) and answer-only faithfulness ($\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$) with fewer flagged refusals ($\TerraFlaggedRefusals$ vs.\ $\HippoFlaggedRefusals$), but answer-only scores are conditional on different answered subsets. On multi-hop reasoning TERRA leads HippoRAG by $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ ($q=\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGAdjQ$). Future benchmark protocols must mandate disentangled reporting of refusal rates alongside answer-only faithfulness.
    \item \textbf{Evaluation Rubric Resolution and Likert Normalization:} Coarse evaluation scales (e.g., discrete binary pass/fail or $\{0.0, 0.8, 1.0\}$ heuristics) induce artificial ceiling compression, clustering over $75\%$ of responses at $1.0$. Implementing a 5-point Likert scale normalized to $[0, 1]$ effectively resolves this compression, exposing genuine variances in doctrinal nuance.
    \item \textbf{Jurisdictional and Temporal Corpus Boundaries:} The pre-built Event Evolution Graph is anchored in \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic substantive U.S. Supreme Court opinions spanning \CorpusTemporalSpan, encompassing seven doctrinal domains of federal jurisprudence (Table~\ref{tab:corpus_stats}). Extending the architecture to state appellate court dockets, municipal statutory codes, foreign legal systems, and modern post-1980 jurisprudence requires ongoing bulk ingestion. Furthermore, while Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability} empirically demonstrates graph traversal stability across temporal snapshot expansions ($T \to T+N$), live vector index insertion and streaming graph maintenance remain unaddressed engineering extensions.
    \item \label{item:hosted-api-determinism}\textbf{Hosted API Output Variability at $T=0.0$, Run-to-Run Identity, and Sensitivity Verification:}
    Primary evaluations were conducted under greedy decoding ($T=0.0$) using \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} and \texttt{databricks-gemma-3-12b}. While setting $T=0.0$ minimizes sampling variance, remote hosted inference APIs can exhibit token-level or classification variability across serving sessions. Across benchmark evaluations, query \texttt{D066} exhibited an empirical classification shift (EASY $\to$ HARD), consistent with numerical or serving-level variability in hosted inference; the precise backend cause cannot be isolated from available logs. Comparing two 14-September TERRA executions across the 350-query benchmark suite, exact string-identical generated answers occurred on \TerraIdenticalAnswerFraction\ of queries overall (206/350), with pronounced category divergence: \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatA\ on Category~A (95/100) and \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatC\ on Category~C (62/75), versus \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatD\ on Category~D (39/75) and \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatB\ on Category~B (10/100). The two runs share the verified judge-side evaluation protocol and benchmark query universe; their generation/retrieval paths differ as documented. Both runs were evaluated under the standardized dual-judge protocol (\texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} and \texttt{databricks-gpt-oss-120b}) using the frozen RAG prompt template (SHA256: \texttt{6d18fc14\dots}) and normalized Likert rubric. Sensitivity verification on an 80B model (\texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct}) across a separate 15-query subset (10 Cat~B, 5 Cat~D; distinct from the firewall stress test in Section~\ref{subsec:benchmark-design}) confirmed invariant relative rankings: TERRA achieved $1.000$ Category~B Faithfulness (vs. $0.900$ Flat RAG, $0.800$ Direct LLM) and $100\%$ Category~D safety rejection (vs. $40\%$ Flat RAG, $0\%$ Direct LLM). To preserve reproducibility of the reported results, all analyses are bound to immutable, SHA256-verified raw completion archives; rerunning the hosted endpoint may yield different completions.
    \item \textbf{Parametric Pretraining Confounders, Latent Weights, and Temporal Containment Bounds:} On continuous evaluation of Category D (Adversarial Deception), Direct LLM recorded a higher continuous Faithfulness score ($\DirectLLMCatDFaithfulness$ vs. $\TerraCatDFaithfulness$), yielding a non-significant Wilcoxon signed-rank comparison in Direct LLM's favor ($\Delta = -0.083, p = 0.0629$, Table~\ref{tab:full_fdr_family}, Rank 11). Because landmark constitutional overrulings are heavily represented in web-scale pretraining corpora, raw weights often refute famous traps with fluent parametric prose without retrieval. However, evaluating discrete outcome safety via the formal rubric (Section~\ref{subsec:benchmark-design}, Table~\ref{tab:refusal_breakdown}) reveals that Direct LLM achieves its $94.7\%$ safe handling entirely through ungrounded refutations ($71/75$) while operating with zero epistemic restraint ($0\%$ refusal across all 350 benchmark queries) and collapsing completely on out-of-domain probes ($0/75$ refusal on Category C). In contrast, TERRA achieves $\mathbf{\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate}$ total safe handling ($73/75$: $\TerraCatDRejection$ explicit refusals and $\TerraCatDRefutations$ verified refutations), delivering a $+\TerraCatDRejectionRate$ explicit refusal advantage ($p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDRefusalMcNemarP$), perfect monotonic containment ($c=0$), and an $80.0\%$ reduction in fatal constraint violations (from $10/75$ to $\TerraCatDFatalErrors$) with zero uncommitted hedges ($0/75$). While the pre-specified hypothesis test in Table~\ref{tab:full_fdr_family} (Rank 11) evaluates continuous faithfulness, TERRA's true structural advantage lies in verifiable citation provenance, epistemic restraint, and temporal boundary integrity. Forensic auditing reveals that the two remaining fatal errors (queries D033 and D034) are reciprocal misattributions between coupled apportionment landmarks (\textit{Baker v. Carr} [1962] and \textit{Reynolds v. Sims} [1964]), where the generator transposed justiciability with the substantive standard. Adaptive edge-weighting to prioritize invalidation paths constitutes essential future work. Similarly, on Category~B (Evolutionary Precedents), Direct LLM achieves higher judge-scored faithfulness ($\DirectLLMCatBFaithfulness$ vs.\ $\TerraCatBFaithfulness$, $\Delta=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$, $q=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$), consistent with base model fluency on generic historical narratives, whereas TERRA's retrieval evaluation shows stronger Category~B citation coverage and full-precedent-path recovery ($\CatBTerraMacroCitationRecall$ macro citation recall vs.\ $\CatBDirectMacroCitationRecall$ for Direct LLM; Section~\ref{subsec:citation-correctness}).

More fundamentally, we distinguish \textit{latent parametric knowledge} from \textit{operative doctrinal leakage}. Because modern foundation models are pretrained on web-scale text, weights encode post-$T$ legal history (e.g., \textit{Plessy} overruled by \textit{Brown} in 1954). TERRA does not purge latent weights; its provenance-bounded retrieval and temporal gate prevent latent memory from intruding into operative pre-$T$ reasoning. While forensic auditing (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}) confirms suppression of Level-2 leakage in $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$, future work should explore circuit editing and machine unlearning for weight-level guarantees. Provider-side safety filtering on historical legal topics (terminating 85 evaluations in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}) highlights the operational dependency of LLM-as-a-judge pipelines on third-party API policies, motivating our sensitivity-bounded framework. Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization} tests this confounder directly: on obscure overruled precedents Direct LLM safe handling was \ObscDirectSafePct\ (\ObscCrossDirectFamousSafe\ on the famous subset), consistent with famous-landmark performance partly reflecting parametric memory.
    \item \textbf{Fixed Graph Traversal Horizon and Multi-Hop Boundary Limits:} TERRA's online retrieval operates with a calibrated 2-hop BFS graph expansion radius to bound latency and token overhead. While 2-hop traversal captures direct citing and invalidating authorities across most evolutionary arcs, it can miss subsequent modifying precedents when citation chains exceed two steps. An empirical boundary emerged during our CaseFacts audit on \textit{Chimel v. California} (query \texttt{CF\_INC\_058}; Section~\ref{subsec:casefacts-generalization}), where the modifying precedent (\textit{United States v. Robinson} [1973]) sat beyond the 2-hop boundary; the generator cited \textit{Chimel}'s 1969 wingspan doctrine but found no modifying precedent in context. This multi-hop horizon likewise accounts for the gold-precedent omission rate during drafting on CLERC ($\ClercTerraMisapplicationTrackOne$; Section~\ref{subsec:clerc-generalization}), where distant authorities prompted analogical reasoning from historical cases rather than fabrication. Developing adaptive traversal horizons along invalidation paths represents a high-priority architectural extension.
\item \textbf{Oracle Relation Labels, Exact-Title Seeding, and a Bundled Ablation:} In Full TERRA, curated \texttt{OVERRULES} edges are serialized with an explicit relation tag, dedicated heading, expanded excerpt budget, and prompt instruction; obscure benchmark pairs were drawn from these edges. The Full-TERRA advantage on that suite is therefore contingent on curated annotations, and the bundled ablation cannot isolate the tag alone. For named-case queries, seeding relied on exact caption matches (category-filtered vector retrieval returned no candidates), causing two queries to produce empty context and safe-rated refusals, one to omit the overruling case, and two to take the fast path; we evaluated TERRA as deployed and report sensitivity subsets excluding these items. The primary comparison contrasts complete systems, and Direct LLM receives no instruction block. Outcomes are judge-dependent in magnitude, the suite has thirty items, and judges were not fully blind to arm identity.

The seven-domain classification is generated by a deterministic \IssueTwentyTwoTotalLexiconPhrases-phrase rule-based lexicon over truncated texts ($\le \IssueTwentyTwoTextTruncationChars$ characters), inducing four limitations: (1)~\textit{Lexical polysemy}: Keyword matching without contextual disambiguation risks misclassification when terms appear in procedural dicta or dissenting quotes. This paper introduced TERRA, an experimental dual-phase GraphRAG architecture addressing knowledge drift and multi-step legal reasoning on historical SCOTUS jurisprudence (\CorpusTemporalSpan). Structuring \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic decisions (\CorpusPrecedentEdges\ citation edges) with procedural reasoning traces, TERRA enables inference via Traffic Cop routing, BFS traversal, and an NLI grader evaluating retrieved evidence. Benchmarking across \numUniqueQueries\ queries (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations) shows higher Category~B multi-hop faithfulness than Flat Vector RAG, HippoRAG, and GraphRAG ($\Delta$ from $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ to $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$; $q<0.05$), though not over Direct LLM ($\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$); higher overall faithfulness ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$, overlapping CIs; $\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$); and $\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate$ adversarial safe handling ($\TerraCatDRejection$ refusals, \TerraCatDRefutations\ refutations). Constraints include \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors, false refusals on \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries, and reliance on curated overruling annotations (Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization}). Critically, because evaluations rely on automated LLM judges without licensed attorneys (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}), human expert review remains an essential prerequisite for deployment. Citation graphs grounded with procedural traces preserve longitudinal stability (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}) \cite{edge2024graphrag, sun2024thinkongraph, zheng2023judging}.

\title{Unifying Event Evolution Graphs and Reasoning Traces via Semantic Entailment: A Dual-Phase Architecture for Judicial GraphRAG}

The fundamental bottleneck in modern RAG systems arises when navigating complex data landscapes characterized by continuous knowledge drift and multi-step reasoning demands. Real-world data evolves dynamically; consequently, static vector indices inevitably accumulate conflicting, time-stamped versions of the same fact. When queried, standard retrievers surface all of these conflicting versions simultaneously based on semantic similarity, leaving the frozen generative model unable to resolve the chronological authority, which induces severe temporal hallucinations. Furthermore, when processing complex logical derivations, standard pipelines retrieve fragmented textual snippets that sever precedential and doctrinal dependencies, proving entirely insufficient for tasks that require deep, multi-hop reasoning.

Recent advancements have attempted to address these bottlenecks in isolated silos, exposing critical failure modes. While structural graph-based retrievers organize facts chronologically, they act merely as static data foundations lacking the procedural logic to guide multi-hop generative reasoning. Conversely, prior paradigms retrieving intermediate structured reasoning traces significantly enhance logical deduction but remain temporally blind and have been primarily restricted to quantitative domains like mathematics or coding. More critically, current Agentic RAG frameworks rely heavily on corrective evaluators that fail fundamentally on conceptual tasks. Mathematical explainability analyses, such as SHAP, have proven that standard evaluators act merely as superficial named entity alignment detectors, failing to comprehend genuine semantic relevance. Compounding this, existing query routers are largely restricted to rigid, binary-channel systems (e.g., pure dense versus pure sparse search), resulting in severe evidence-intent mismatches when unrestricted search floods the context window with noisy, irrelevant data.

To bridge these isolated gaps, this paper introduces an integrated dual-phase GraphRAG architecture purpose-built for dynamically evolving, knowledge-intensive environments (with empirical graph traversal stability across temporal snapshot expansions evaluated in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}). The proposed system confines all computationally heavy operations to an offline preprocessing phase, constructing a dual-index corpus that cross-links an Event Evolution Graph (EEG)---which encodes chronological precedent relationships across \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic judicial decisions and \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed citation edges---with a node-level procedural reasoning trace database that captures structured legal analysis trajectories (constitutional issue, procedural history, legal test, holding). During online inference, a small language model acts as a Traffic Cop router, dynamically allocating retrieval priority across text chunks, graph subgraphs, and procedural reasoning traces, enabling a bimodal execution profile (median \TerraFastPathMedianSeconds~s on single-point factual lookups vs. \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds~s on multi-hop precedent chains). Before the final response generation, an autonomous semantic entailment grader replaces flawed keyword-matching heuristics, verifying the true conceptual and structural relevance of the retrieved evidence.

\subsection{Summary of Contributions}
The primary contributions of this work are as follows:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{An Authentic Dual-Index Architecture:} We design and implement an authentic dual-index judicial GraphRAG corpus that cross-links a structural Event Evolution Graph (EEG) of \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic SCOTUS decisions (\CorpusPrecedentEdges\ citation edges) with a node-level procedural reasoning trace database, supporting joint chronological and logical evidence alignment with zero synthetic cases.
    \item \textbf{Traffic Cop Routing with Coarse Domain Pre-filtering:} We introduce an SLM-driven complexity router paired with a two-stage coarse proximity pre-filter ($d_{L2} < 1.3$ + Title Match) that provides scale-dependent domain boundary filtering without maintaining static allowlists (empirical coverage and calibration detailed in Section~\ref{subsec:computational-budget} and Section~\ref{subsec:firewall-analysis}).
    \item \textbf{NLI-Based Entailment Evaluation and XAI Attribution:} We replace superficial keyword-matching heuristics with a specialized Natural Language Inference (NLI) grader that evaluates retrieved evidence to intercept ungrounded generations, providing qualitative reasoning traces and citation provenance.
    \item \textbf{Data Leakage Mitigation Framework:} We formalize explicit safeguards against temporal precedent inversion, benchmark retrieval contamination, and cross-domain feature bleeding.
    \item \textbf{Empirical Rigor and Statistical Validation:} Through benchmarking (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations across \numUniqueQueries\ queries $\times$ \numComparativePipelines\ pipelines at $T=0.0$) with paired Wilcoxon tests, Cohen's $d_z$, and 95\% bootstrap CIs, TERRA achieves the highest Answer-Only Faithfulness among RAG architectures ($\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulness$ vs.\ HippoRAG's $\HippoRAGAnswerOnlyFaithfulness$), outperforms Flat Vector RAG ($\Delta = \CatBTerraVsFlatDelta$, $p = \CatBTerraVsFlatWilcoxonP$, $d_z = \CatBTerraVsFlatDz$) and HippoRAG ($\Delta = \CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$, $p = \CatBTerraVsHippoRAGWilcoxonP$, $d_z = \CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDz$) on Category~B reasoning, delivers $\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate$ adversarial safe handling ($\TerraCatDSafeHandling$: \TerraCatDRejection\ refusals, \TerraCatDRefutations\ refutations) with \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors vs.\ $\BaselineFatalMin$--$\BaselineFatalMax$ for baselines, and incurs \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ false refusals on Category~A (\TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ on Category~B). Evaluations rely on automated LLM judges without licensed attorneys, establishing human review as an essential prerequisite (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}).

\section{Related Work and Systematic Taxonomy}
Prior GraphRAG, legal-retrieval, temporal-reasoning, and LLM-evaluation studies motivate TERRA's separation of graph traversal, procedural traces, routing, and entailment verification. The systematic taxonomy and full related-work comparisons are preserved in Supplementary Section~\ref{sec:supp-protocols-prompts}.

To rigorously evaluate TERRA GraphRAG, we adopt an ablation-first empirical methodology. Rather than presenting aggregated metrics that obscure internal component dynamics, we first dissect the architecture into its constituent mechanisms to isolate the empirical contribution of each subsystem. We then evaluate multi-hop evolutionary reasoning via pairwise win rates and semantic faithfulness, examine factual precision and safety firewalling across the complete \numTotalEvals-evaluation benchmark, profile stage-level latency distributions, and conduct formal statistical significance and power audits.

\subsection{Standalone Traffic Cop Classifier Evaluation and Defense-in-Depth}
\label{subsec:router-standalone-eval}

While the component-level ablation in the ablation results establishes the system-level operational necessity of query routing (Ablation~3: forcing all queries into multi-hop GraphRAG traversal causes a $\AblationRouterLatencySlowdownFactor\times$ latency penalty alongside $\AblationThreeCatAFalseRefusalRate$ false refusals on factual lookups), evaluating the router purely as a component in an end-to-end pipeline leaves its intrinsic classification quality unquantified. To resolve this question, we evaluate the Traffic Cop Router as an independent, standalone binary intent classifier across all $N=\RouterTotalQueries$ canonical benchmark queries. All evaluations were executed deterministically at temperature $T=0.0$ using Google Gemma 3 12B Instruction-tuned (\texttt{\RouterModel}) served via the Databricks Model Serving API under strict schema validation (\texttt{RoutingDecision}), with certified zero fallback contamination ($0/350$). \subsubsection{Mechanistic Analysis of Category D Misroutes and Defense-in-Depth}
As disaggregated in Supplementary Table S5 (Panel~B), all 10 queries classified as EASY by the router belong exclusively to Category~D (Adversarial Deception Traps; $\RouterCatDFalseEasyRate$, $\RouterCatDFalseEasyCount/75$). A forensic examination of these 10 queries (\texttt{D021}, \texttt{D039}, \texttt{D060}, \texttt{D062}, \texttt{D068}, \texttt{D069}, \texttt{D070}, \texttt{D072}, \texttt{D073}, \texttt{D074}) reveals a uniform syntactic structure: each query is formulated as a single-sentence constitutional inquiry referencing a single landmark authority (e.g., query \texttt{D021}: \textit{``Did the Supreme Court in Mapp v. Ohio establish that police custodial interrogations must be preceded by four-point constitutional rights warnings?''}). Because these queries lack explicit multi-hop syntactic connectors (such as comparative doctrine tracing across decades), the SLM router classifies them based on surface-level syntactic simplicity as single-case lookups.

Crucially, routing these adversarial queries to the fast path does \textit{not} induce generative hallucination or credulous acceptance of false premises. Under TERRA's Grounded Fast Path (Issue~\#12), fast-path generations are anchored directly against verified procedural holdings rather than ungrounded parametric completion. Forensic auditing of the downstream completions under independent dual judging demonstrates a certified $\mathbf{\RouterCatDSafeHandlingRate}$ safe-handling rate ($10/10$):
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Safe Epistemic Refusals ($8/10$, $80.0\%$):} On 8 queries (\texttt{D021}, \texttt{D039}, \texttt{D060}, \texttt{D062}, \texttt{D069}, \texttt{D072}, \texttt{D073}, \texttt{D074}), the model detected that the factual predicate was ungrounded in verified case law and deterministically refused to answer without fabricating doctrine.
    \item \textbf{Unflagged Textual Refusals ($2/10$, $20.0\%$):} On 2 queries (\texttt{D068} regarding the Lottery Case and \texttt{D070} regarding the oleomargarine tax), the model generated unflagged textual refusals asserting absence or insufficiency of retrieved context without triggering the gate, scoring 1.000 by dual judges.
    \item \textbf{Zero Fatal Violations ($0/10$, $0.0\%$):} Across all 10 misrouted adversarial cases, zero fatal constraint violations were observed.
\end{itemize}
This empirical result proves the effectiveness of TERRA's multi-tier defense-in-depth architecture: even when an adversarial input slips past the front-line small language model router via deceptive single-sentence syntax, downstream grounding mechanisms reliably prevent hallucination and safeguard epistemic integrity.

\subsection{Temporal Parametric Leakage Stress Test}
\label{subsec:temporal-leakage}

While retrospective legal retrieval requires evaluating questions strictly under historical jurisprudence as of temporal cutoff $T$, modern generative language models possess extensive pretraining corpora containing post-$T$ legal history. Consequently, models risk emitting \textit{temporal parametric leakage}---anachronistically importing future doctrinal shifts, statutory overhauls, or later overrulings into historical analyses. To rigorously quantify and stress-test this vulnerability, we preregistered and executed a dedicated 50-query temporal leakage probe across five historical Supreme Court horizons ($T \in \{1890, 1930, 1950, 1970, 1980\}$), spanning seven major doctrinal domains and balanced across case prominence and multi-hop reasoning depths. Six probes (12\%) targeting historical cases decided between 1857 and 1905 (evaluated at cutoffs $T=1890$ and $T=1930$) have target nodes with zero out-edges in the EEG due to the corpus citation-parsing boundary. Arc evolution cases for these entries are historically verified against primary legal sources but are not EEG graph edges. All leakage metrics are computed identically across all 50 probes regardless of arc status.

\subsubsection{Experimental Design and Metric Decoupling}
The probe evaluates \TemporalTotalEvaluations\ responses generated across four comparative architectures: Direct LLM, Flat Vector RAG, $\text{TERRA}_{\text{ungated}}$ ($L_{\text{gen}}$), and $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ ($L_{\text{final}}$). To separate baseline capabilities from prompt compliance, each architecture is tested under two distinct regimes: \textbf{Condition A} (standard task prompt without explicit temporal constraint, measuring default end-to-end containment) and \textbf{Condition B} (explicit instruction to strictly adhere to year $T$ and ignore future precedents, measuring prompt-assisted containment). All candidate generations were evaluated under a preregistered 3-tier severity rubric: Level~0 (clean adherence to pre-$T$ doctrine), Level~1 (non-prejudicial historical mention or temporal disclaimer), and Level~2 (fatal substantive reliance on post-$T$ law). The primary metric, \textbf{Substantive Post-$T$ Leakage Rate (SPTLR)}, captures the proportion of Level~2 fatal failures.

Critically, evaluating temporal containment solely via SPTLR creates a severe vulnerability to metric distortion: systems that simply refuse to answer generate zero post-$T$ text, appearing perfectly ``leak-free'' despite failing the underlying legal task. To eliminate this confound, we decouple containment from legal problem-solving by measuring: (1)~\textbf{Refusal Rate}, isolating epistemic or safety rejections; and (2)~\textbf{Historical Legal Correctness Rate (HLCR)}, assessing whether the system correctly articulates the operative contemporaneous rule as of year $T$. Finally, we measure the \textbf{NLI Gate Leakage Interception Rate (NGLIR)}, defined as the proportion of ungated candidate leaks intercepted by the entailment gate on the conditioning denominator of leaking candidates ($D$).

\subsubsection{Evaluator Reliability, Concordance, and Consensus Protocol}
Responses were independently evaluated by two distinct model-based judges: \texttt{qwen3-next-80b} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}. Across $N=\TemporalValidPairs$ complete pairs, the evaluators achieved $\TemporalRawConcordance$ raw concordance and $100\%$ monotonic inclusion (every leak identified by GPT-OSS was a strict subset of Qwen's flags). However, the quadratic weighted Cohen's $\kappa$ was $\TemporalQwk$, appearing considerably lower than the benchmark-wide agreement ($\kappa \approx 0.70$). Forensic diagnosis confirms that this divergence is an artifact of the \textit{Kappa Paradox}~\cite{feinstein1990high}: GPT-OSS exhibited a severe $91.7\%$ base-rate skew toward Level~0 ($289/315$ clean), which mechanically inflated expected chance agreement $P_e$ to $\approx 60\%$, deflating $\kappa$ despite high raw agreement. Furthermore, qualitative analysis revealed an evaluator threshold asymmetry: Qwen operated as a hyper-vigilant lexical scanner (flagging any passing historical reference as Level~1 or Level~2), whereas GPT-OSS evaluated holistic legal operability (classifying responses as clean if post-$T$ references did not alter the substantive legal outcome).

To guarantee objective reproducibility, all evaluations were reconciled via a pre-specified, deterministic 5-tier consensus protocol: (1)~safe refusals automatically resolve to Level~0; (2)~unanimous agreement is preserved; (3)~lexical breach of forbidden historical phrases assigns Level~2; (4)~substantive quotation of post-$T$ law assigns Level~2; and (5)~subtle mentions resolve conservatively to $\max(s_1, s_2) = \text{Level~1}$. Crucially, tiers 3--5 bias strictly \textit{toward} flagging leakage, ensuring that consensus adjudication is conservative against TERRA.

\subsubsection{Empirical Missingness Mechanism and Sensitivity Bounds}
Among the $400$ evaluations, $85$ GPT-OSS calls suffered provider-side safety filter terminations. To determine whether this missingness introduced bias, we audited failure distribution across queries and domains. Missingness was strongly non-random: failures clustered heavily in Intellectual Property/Patents ($32.1\%$, $18/56$), Antitrust ($23.2\%$, $13/56$), and Commerce ($23.2\%$, $13/56$). Furthermore, Direct LLM accounted for $30$ of the $85$ missing evaluations, concentrated on queries with high potential for blatant modern citation. Because safety filters disproportionately suppressed Direct LLM's most egregious leakage instances, complete-case Direct LLM leakage ($28.0\%$ in Condition A) is an underestimate. To maintain absolute statistical honesty, Supplementary Table S6 reports full sensitivity bounds $[SPTLR_{\text{lower}}, SPTLR_{\text{upper}}]$ encompassing all $2^{85}$ missing-data assignments, alongside complete $(b, c)$ discordant-pair reporting for all hypotheses.

\subsubsection{Primary Hypothesis $H_1$: Metric Decoupling and Refusal Masking}
Discordant pairs are defined in standard McNemar form: $b$ denotes query pairs where $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ is clean (Level~0 or Level~1) while the baseline exhibits Level~2 substantive leakage; $c$ denotes query pairs where $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ exhibits Level~2 leakage while the baseline is clean. For each comparison, Supplementary Table S6 reports both the un-imputed complete-case pairs ($N_{\text{cc}}$, where both judges completed evaluation under the 5-tier consensus protocol) and the full $N=50$ sensitivity bounds ($[b_{\min}, b_{\max}], [c_{\min}, c_{\max}]$ adding bounded missing-pair additions across all $2^{85}$ feasible permutations).

Preregistered Primary Hypothesis $H_1$ predicted that under default prompting (Condition A), $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ would achieve lower raw SPTLR than Flat Vector RAG. As reported in Supplementary Table S6, this hypothesis is \textbf{not supported}. Under complete cases ($N_{\text{cc}}=36$), consensus yields $b=0, c=3$ (one-sided exact McNemar $p = \HoneSptlrPval$; two-sided $p=0.2500$, or $p=0.0625$ if missing records are zero-imputed at $N=50$). Bounding over all missingness permutations yields $b \in [0, 5], c \in [7, 8]$. Flat Vector RAG exhibits a lower raw leakage interval ($\FlatRagSptlrA$) than $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ ($\TerraGatedSptlrA$).

However, forensic examination of discordant pairs reveals the exact mechanistic origin of this result: Flat RAG produced zero leaks on queries where TERRA was clean ($b=0$) because Flat RAG suffered a massive $\FlatRagRefusalA$ refusal collapse ($23/50$ queries), completely abdicating on nearly half the dataset. When a retrieval system refuses to answer, it mechanically cannot leak post-$T$ doctrine. Conversely, TERRA attempted and successfully engaged with these difficult historical inquiries (refusal rate $\TerraGatedRefusalA$), incurring $c=3$ complete-case Level-2 classifications on complex multi-jurisdictional tests where Flat RAG simply refused.

When evaluating substantive legal utility via Historical Legal Correctness Rate (HLCR), TERRA significantly outperforms Flat Vector RAG: $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ achieves $\mathbf{\TerraGatedHlcrA}$ consensus correctness compared to only $\FlatRagHlcrA$ for Flat RAG ($b=20, c=1$; exact McNemar $p = \HoneHlcrPvalFormatted$, $p < 0.0001$). Thus, TERRA effectively doubles reliable historical legal competence, and its apparent raw SPTLR parity in Condition A is solely an artifact of Flat RAG's refusal volume masking.

\subsection{External Benchmark Generalization and Anti-Circularity Audit (CaseFacts)}
\label{subsec:casefacts-generalization}

While the canonical \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark rigorously probes multi-hop temporal evolution within indexed Supreme Court jurisprudence, evaluating exclusively on researcher-constructed queries introduces potential risks of circular alignment or latent benchmark overfitting. To establish out-of-distribution empirical validity, we evaluate TERRA against an independent, third-party benchmark: \textbf{CaseFacts} \cite{putta2026casefactsbenchmarklegalfactchecking}, a legal fact-checking dataset constructed from U.S. Supreme Court decisions by an external research team.

All 510 evaluations ($360$ Track 1, $150$ Track 2 across Direct LLM, Flat Vector RAG, and Full TERRA) were executed under strict payload parity ($T=0.0$, max tokens 4096, identical LLaMA 3.3 70B generator) and evaluated by independent, non-LLaMA dual judges (\texttt{qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}). Evaluators achieved $100.0\%$ concordance on parsed classification labels with certified zero LLaMA fallback contaminations.

\subsection{Standardized External Benchmark Evaluation on CLERC (NAACL 2025)}
\label{subsec:clerc-generalization}

While the internal \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark rigorously isolates specific algorithmic mechanisms (Sections~\ref{subsec:safety-and-factual}--\ref{subsec:ablation-study}) and CaseFacts establishes external fact-checking and overruling recognition (Section~\ref{subsec:casefacts-generalization}), evaluating on researcher-crafted queries leaves open whether the architecture generalizes to standardized legal retrieval and generative drafting benchmarks designed by independent natural language processing teams. To address this question, we evaluate TERRA on a stratified sample of \textbf{CLERC} (\textit{Case Law Evaluation and Retrieval Corpus}; Findings of NAACL 2025) \cite{hou2024clerc}, a standardized legal benchmark constructed by Johns Hopkins University and collaborating institutions.

\paragraph{Provenance Audit and Seed Purge}
To guard against latent circularity, we executed an automated cryptographic provenance audit. Out of 120 Track 1 target cases, exactly zero ($0.0\%$, 0/120) overlap with the 34 hand-curated landmark seed nodes that received bespoke reasoning traces during graph construction; all overlapping queries were purged during split generation. Track 1 evaluates on a certified $100.0\%$ uncurated graph substrate. Crucially, this exclusion specifically guarantees that evaluation is not artificially aided by the bespoke reasoning-trace seeds created during system development; it does not preclude legitimate retrieval over ordinary authentic Supreme Court opinions in the 20,000-opinion corpus, which serves as the uniform, shared knowledge substrate for all evaluated retrieval systems. As a documented limitation and scope distinction, the broader corpus-wide substantive holding extraction cascade (Tier~1 syllabi and Tier~2 headnotes covering $51.1\%$ of the 20,000 opinions) was not separately screened, as it constitutes the uniform, automated knowledge substrate available to all in-corpus GraphRAG retrievers.

\paragraph{Pre-Flight Gate Smoke Test}
Following the fatal-interception safeguards developed in prior evaluation phases, the batch harness enforces a mandatory pre-flight assertion over three known-refusal probes (Probe 1: Modern Post-1980 Authority; Probe 2: Fabricated Holding Trap; Probe 3: Non-SCOTUS Circuit Rule). The harness verifies that the NLI Smart Grader successfully short-circuits execution before launching the full evaluation batch.

\paragraph{Independent Non-LLaMA Dual Judging}
All completions across Direct LLM, Flat Vector RAG, and Full TERRA were executed under strict payload parity ($T=0.0$, max tokens 4096, identical LLaMA 3.3 70B generator) and judged by independent, non-LLaMA dual evaluators (\texttt{qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}). Exact citation metrics (Citation Precision and Citation Recall) were computed via deterministic parse-tree resolution using \texttt{eyecite}.

\subsection{Direct Evidence Retrieval Quality and Precedent-Chain Coverage}
\label{subsec:retrieval-quality}

A critical question in retrieval-augmented legal architectures is whether downstream generative advantages stem from superior evidence retrieval or merely reflect the generator's ability to synthesize plausible analyses from average context. Furthermore, Second Review Issue~\#11 noted that while TERRA's canonical graph expansion operates with breadth $k=2$ and depth $d=2$, Category~B queries comprise 3-to-5 node evolutionary arcs (spanning 2 to 4 citation hops), requiring explicit evaluation of retrieval success as a function of precedent chain length.

The core judicial benchmark encompasses $N=350$ queries across four operational strata: Category~A ($N=100$ single-point factual lookups), Category~B ($N=100$ multi-hop evolutionary chains), Category~C ($N=75$ out-of-context unanswerable refusal probes where target authorities are absent from the corpus, evaluated for gate interception in Section~\ref{subsec:safety-and-factual}), and Category~D ($N=75$ adversarial temporal overruling pairs). To rigorously isolate evidence-retrieval quality on complex multi-hop common-law reasoning without conflating single-point lookups (which TERRA intentionally routes through its parametric Fast Path) or unanswerable negative probes (where no target nodes exist in the corpus), we evaluate raw evidence retrieval on the $N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ Category~B multi-hop trajectories ($\CatBGoldPrecedents$ gold landmark precedents) prior to generator invocation.

Because comparative architectures deliver heterogeneous retrieval representations---Flat Vector RAG returns a linear ranked list of document chunks, GraphRAG delivers unranked modularity community reports, HippoRAG yields unranked Personalized PageRank (PPR) activation clusters, and TERRA produces a 2-hop directed EEG subgraph structured by temporal edges and holding headnotes---linear ranked-list metrics such as MRR or nDCG cannot be applied uniformly across community and subgraph representations without imposing arbitrary ranking assumptions. We therefore evaluate deterministic dual-resolution entity recall (exact CAP Node ID and canonical case title) and full precedent trajectory recovery in Supplementary Table S10. All retrieval metrics are evaluated directly on the canonical stored \texttt{context\_full} fields from \texttt{terra\_baselines\_eval\_raw.json} (SHA256 verified) that were delivered to the LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct generator in the primary dual-judge benchmark, guaranteeing zero retrieval drift or post-hoc re-extraction divergence.

\subsubsection{Formal Definition and Seed Positioning of Multi-Seed Anchoring}
The ability of TERRA's nominal $d=2$ graph traversal to achieve complete path recovery on 3-hop and 4-hop lineages is governed by \textit{multi-seed anchoring}. For an evolutionary query $q$, entity and legal concept extraction identifies a set of seed nodes $S_q \subset V$ with $|S_q| \ge 2$ (empirical mean of $\CatBMeanSeedsPerQuery$ seeds per query across Category~B; $\CatBTwoSeedsPct$ with $|S_q|=2$, $\CatBThreeSeedsPct$ with $|S_q|=3$, and $\CatBFourPlusSeedsPct$ with $|S_q| \ge 4$). From each seed $s \in S_q$, directed EEG traversal expands a $d=2$ graph ball $B(s, 2)$ along forward and backward citation edges with breadth $k=2$.

Crucially, empirical auditing of seed placements confirms that multi-seed extraction anchors the extremities of the precedent trajectory: in $\CatBEndpointsAnchoredPct$ of 5-node chains (5/5) and $\CatBFourNodeEndpointsAnchoredPct$ of recovered 4-node chains (20/20), seeds anchor both the historical origin (index 0) and the culminating modern authority (index $m-1$). For an evolutionary chain $v_0 \to \dots \to v_{m-1}$, the forward 2-hop ball $B(v_0, 2)$ covers $\{v_0, v_1, v_2\}$ while the reverse 2-hop ball $B(v_{m-1}, 2)$ covers $\{v_{m-1}, v_{m-2}, v_{m-3}\}$. \subsection{Computational Budget Profiling and Geometric Gate Calibration}
\label{subsec:computational-budget}

A rigorous comparative evaluation of complex agentic RAG frameworks requires auditing the full computational footprint of the underlying architecture. Second Review Issue~\#10 noted that multi-stage RAG pipelines deploy multiple sequential inference calls (query routing, vector retrieval, graph traversal, NLI verification, and final generation), which can compound latency, token consumption, and serving costs. To provide complete transparency and establish call parity against standard single-shot baselines, Supplementary Table S12 profiles total operations per query, active 70B generator invocations, end-to-end and decoupled component latencies, effective token volumes, and financial costs across all \numComparativePipelines\ comparative architectures, alongside an empirical calibration of the Tier~2 geometric pre-filter on the 20,000-case CAP index.

Critically, both Category~C (unanswerable out-of-domain probes) and Category~D (adversarial overruling pairs) operate under an identical deterministic self-correction mechanism:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Passing Entailment (Attempt~1 Resolution):} Queries that satisfy NLI entailment on the initial attempt require $1\text{ retrieval} + 1\text{ NLI verification} + 1\text{ generator invocation} = 4\text{ operations}$. This path is taken by $\TerraCatCPassNliGenCount$ queries in Category~C ($\TerraCatCPassNliGenCount \times 4 = \TerraCatCPassNliOps\text{ operations}$) and $\TerraCatDPassNliGenCount$ queries in Category~D ($\TerraCatDPassNliGenCount \times 4 = \TerraCatDPassNliOps\text{ operations}$).
    \item \textbf{Failing Entailment (Attempt~2 Halting):} Queries failing entailment on Attempt~1 trigger an expanded retrieval query and undergo a second NLI verification attempt; when Attempt~2 likewise fails, generation halts in a deterministic safety refusal ($2\text{ retrievals} + 2\text{ NLI verifications} + 0\text{ generator invocations} = 5\text{ operations}$). This trajectory is executed by $\TerraCatCFailNliHaltedCount$ post-retrieval halted queries in Category~C ($\TerraCatCFailNliHaltedCount \times 5 = \TerraCatCFailNliOps\text{ operations}$) and $\TerraCatDFailNliHaltedCount$ post-retrieval halted queries in Category~D ($\TerraCatDFailNliHaltedCount \times 5 = \TerraCatDFailNliOps\text{ operations}$).
    \item \textbf{Pre-Retrieval Interceptions (Category~C):} In Category~C, $\TerraCatCPreFilterExceedingHaltedCount$ out-of-domain queries exceed the geometric proximity boundary ($d_{L2} \ge 1.30$) and are terminated immediately pre-retrieval, incurring only $1\text{ operation}$ each ($\TerraCatCPreFilterExceedingHaltedCount \times 1 = \TerraCatCPreFilterHaltedOps\text{ operations}$). A single borderline probe (\texttt{C069}, $d_{L2}=1.366$) proceeds directly to the generator with empty context ($1\text{ pre-filter} + 1\text{ generator} = \TerraCatCBorderlineOps\text{ operations}$).
\end{itemize}
Summing these operational paths yields exact integer closure: $\TerraCatCPreFilterHaltedOps + \TerraCatCBorderlineOps + \TerraCatCFailNliOps + \TerraCatCPassNliOps = \TerraCatCTotalOps\text{ operations}$ on Category~C (averaging $\TerraCatCTotalOpsPerQuery$ ops/query) and $\TerraCatDFailNliOps + \TerraCatDPassNliOps = \TerraCatDTotalOps\text{ operations}$ on Category~D (averaging $\TerraCatDTotalOpsPerQuery$ ops/query). Combined with Category~A ($\TerraCatATotalOps\text{ operations}$) and Category~B ($\TerraCatBTotalOps\text{ operations}$), TERRA executes $\TerraBenchmarkTotalOpsFormatted\text{ operations}$ ($\TerraOverallTotalOpsPerQuery$ ops/query).

Importantly, while TERRA executes more sequential pipeline stages than single-shot baselines, it invokes the computationally expensive 70B parameter generator on only $\TerraOverallGenCallsCount$ of the 350 benchmark queries ($\TerraOverallGenCallsPct$), achieving a $\TerraOverallGenCallsReductionPct$ reduction in active 70B generator calls compared to comparative baselines ($350/350$). This reduction is driven by epistemic refusal on Category~C ($\TerraCatCGenCallsFormatted$) and adversarial safety halting on Category~D ($\TerraCatDGenCallsFormatted$). We frame this generator-call reduction not as an alternative metric for call parity, but as one important mitigating factor in aggregate serving efficiency.

\subsubsection{Candid Disclosure of Deliberate Latency and Cost Trade-Offs}
Operating a multi-stage sequential architecture entails a deliberate engineering trade-off between computational budget and epistemic reliability. On complex multi-hop evolutionary chains (Category~B), TERRA exhibits a median pipeline latency of $\TerraHardPathMedianSeconds\text{ s}$ ($\TerraCatBLatencyMeanMS\text{ ms}$ mean) and an operational cost of $\TerraCatBTotalCostPerThousand$ per 1,000 queries ($\TerraCatBPerQueryCost$ per query), compared to $\FlatRAGLatencyMedMS\text{ ms}$ and $\FlatRAGTotalCostPerThousand$ per 1,000 queries ($\FlatRAGPerQueryCost$ per query) for Flat Vector RAG---representing a $\TerraCatBVsFlatCostRatio$ per-query cost ratio.

We candidly disclose this computational overhead as an intentional, necessary investment to resolve the structural vulnerabilities of dense semantic retrieval. As established in Section~\ref{subsec:retrieval-quality}, Flat Vector RAG achieves only $\CatBFlatFullPathRecall$ full precedent path recovery ($\CatBFlatFullPathCount$), collapsing completely on three-hop and four-hop legal trajectories. In contrast, TERRA's coordinated EEG citation traversal and procedural trace synthesis attains $\CatBTerraFullPathRecall$ complete precedent path recovery ($\CatBTerraFullPathCount$), delivering a $\CatBTerraVsFlatPathRecallFactor$ increase in trajectory recovery over Flat RAG. In high-stakes legal applications where ungrounded generative hallucinations or missing precedent stepping-stones induce malpractice liability, expending $\sim \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds\text{ s}$ and approximately one cent per query to secure complete doctrinal authority is an operationally sound trade-off.

\subsubsection{Tier 2 Geometric Domain Boundary Pre-Filter Calibration}
Supplementary Table S12 (Panel~B) presents empirical calibration for the Tier~2 geometric proximity pre-filter across distance thresholds $\tau \in [0.90, 1.40]$ on the 20,000-case CAP index, evaluated against $N=200$ in-domain legal queries (Categories~A and B) and $N=75$ out-of-domain probes (Category~C).

The isolated pre-filter demonstrates strong discriminative separation, achieving an AUROC of $\TerraGateIsolatedAUROC$. At aggressive thresholds ($\tau \le 1.10$), the filter rejects out-of-domain queries at high rates ($\TerraGateTPRTauZeroNineZero$ at $\tau=0.90$) but induces unacceptable false refusals on legitimate constitutional inquiries ($\TerraGateFPRTauZeroNineZero$, $\TerraGateFPRCountTauZeroNineZero$). As the threshold relaxes to $\tau=1.25$ and $\tau=1.30$, in-domain false refusals collapse to zero ($\TerraGateFPRTauOneThreeZero$, $\TerraGateFPRCountTauOneThreeZero$).

Under TERRA's operational threshold $\tau=1.30$, the pre-filter functions with zero false refusal while intercepting $\TerraGateTPRTauOneThreeZero$ ($\TerraGateTPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) of out-of-domain probes before retrieval. The remaining $\TerraGateFNRTauOneThreeZero$ ($\TerraGateFNRCountTauOneThreeZero$) of out-of-domain queries slip past the pre-filter and enter retrieval; however, these deferred queries are subsequently intercepted by downstream NLI entailment grading, which halts generation in a safe refusal. We emphasize that geometric proximity serves strictly as an \textit{optional coarse pre-filter} to conserve retrieval and grading compute on obvious out-of-domain inputs; embedding distance metrics do not prove legal validity or domain membership, which remains the exclusive operational responsibility of the downstream NLI Smart Grader.

\subsection{Benchmark-Graph Traversal Stability Under Temporal Snapshot Expansion}
\label{subsec:temporal-update-stability}

To evaluate precedent traversal stability under corpus growth without generative confounding, we test standalone breadth-first graph traversal across four chronological snapshot expansions: $1890\to1930$ (Pair~I, Step $N=40$~yr), $1930\to1950$ (Pair~II, Step $N=20$~yr), $1950\to1970$ (Pair~III, Step $N=20$~yr), and $1970\to1980$ (Pair~IV, Step $N=10$~yr).

Across $N=\IssueNineteenTotalEvals$ qualifying Category~B observations ($\IssueNineteenUniqueQueries$ unique queries anchored at an origin precedent decided at or before Year~$T$, with at least one subsequent gold authority in $(T, T+N]$), BFS citation traversal ($k=2, d=2$, matching production parameters) was run on base subgraph $G_{\le T}$ and expanded subgraph $G_{\le T+N}$ seeded by benchmark origin precedent ($s = q[\texttt{target\_nodes}][0]$). As reported in Supplementary Table S13, expanding from $T$ to $T+N$ shifts grand pooled recall from $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTMeanStd$ to $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTNMeanStd$ ($\Delta\text{Recall} = \IssueNineteenOverallDeltaRecallMeanStd$), with $\IssueNineteenStabilityCoefficient$ of queries exhibiting non-negative recall shift ($\Delta\text{Recall} \ge 0$). On newly eligible authorities ($S_{\text{new}}$), traversal attains a grand mean Discovery Rate of $\IssueNineteenDiscoveryRateMean$, with median traversal latency under one millisecond (\IssueNineteenBFSLatencyMedianMs~ms; grand mean $0.15 \pm 0.18$~ms). Three methodological boundaries govern these findings: (1)~Because gold sequences include seed anchor $s$ (retrieved at depth 0), absolute recall reflects baseline seed inclusion; $\Delta\text{Recall}$ is invariant to this offset. (2)~Negative shifts on specific queries stem from degree caps when expanding nodes become hubs. (3)~This standalone experiment evaluates topological traversal over available directed edges (generic \texttt{CITES}) on NetworkX DiGraphs; it is decoupled from upstream vector retrieval (subject to the category filter limitation in Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}) and does not evaluate live vector index upsert, which remains future systems engineering.

The empirical evaluation validates that TERRA addresses fundamental failure modes of standard RAG architectures in knowledge-intensive, dynamic environments. This section contextualizes our primary architectural contributions, candidly examines current system limitations, and outlines future research directions.

\subsection{Empirical Analysis of Firewall Component Contributions and Scale Dynamics}
\label{subsec:firewall-analysis}

A critical finding from our systematic post-hoc auditing concerns the empirical division of labor within TERRA's safety architecture. The original design conceptualized the Domain Boundary Firewall as an active two-stage pre-retrieval filter where vector distance ($d_{L2} < 1.3$) flags out-of-domain (OOD) queries before graph traversal. However, systematic auditing across the preliminary 50-query Category C audit set on the initial 10,009-opinion index revealed that the vector proximity gate was non-functional at this scale ($0/50$ intercepted) because unconstrained OOD distances ($0.281 \le d_{L2} \le 0.859$) fell entirely beneath $1.3$.

Consequently, safety performance in Table~\ref{tab:overall_summary} (\TerraCatCRejectionRate\ refusal on Category C, \TerraCatDRejectionRate\ refusal and $\TerraCatDRefutationRate$\ verified refutation on Category D) was delivered almost entirely by the downstream NLI Smart Grader (Tier 3) via double-failure refusal. When OOD queries entered retrieval, the resulting lack of semantic entailment triggered a safe refusal. Removing NLI in ablation (the ablation results, Ablation 2) caused an immediate collapse of adversarial safety to 0.0\%, confirming NLI as the true empirical safeguard.

Crucially, empirical calibration on the expanded 20,000-opinion substantive corpus demonstrates that geometric pre-filtering exhibits scale- and density-dependent behavior. As reported in Supplementary Table S12 (Panel~B), evaluating the full $N=75$ Category~C benchmark suite against the 20k index yields an isolated AUROC of $\TerraGateIsolatedAUROC$. At the operational threshold $\tau = 1.30$, geometric pre-filtering achieves $\TerraGateFPRTauOneThreeZero$ in-domain false refusal ($\TerraGateFPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) while intercepting $\TerraGateTPRTauOneThreeZero$ ($\TerraGateTPRCountTauOneThreeZero$) of out-of-domain probes pre-retrieval. Comparing the 10k index (where 50/50 probes fell below $1.3$) to the 20k index (where 41/75 probes exceed $1.3$) reflects an empirical observation of corpus manifold density: expanding corpus volume across seven verified constitutional domains creates denser semantic clustering, pushing extraneous out-of-domain queries farther into the embedding margin. We do not assert any generalized theoretical scaling law from these two empirical corpus snapshots; rather, we treat geometric proximity strictly as an optional coarse pre-filter that saves retrieval and NLI compute on obvious outliers, while downstream NLI entailment verification serves as the indispensable primary safety firewall.

To ensure complete scientific transparency and maintain the highest standard of academic integrity, we identify eighteen methodological limitations of the current architecture, grouped into five cohesive thematic subsections (with unabridged registers provided in Supplementary Sections S2.1--S2.18):

\noindent\textbf{Evaluation Rubric Resolution and Likert Normalization (Limitation~3):} Coarse evaluation scales (e.g., discrete binary pass/fail or $\{0.0, 0.8, 1.0\}$ heuristics) induce artificial ceiling compression, clustering over $75\%$ of responses at $1.0$. Implementing a 5-point Likert scale normalized to $[0, 1]$ effectively resolves this compression, exposing genuine variances in doctrinal nuance.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.3.}

\noindent\textbf{Hosted API Output Variability at $T=0.0$, Run-to-Run Identity, and Sensitivity Verification (Limitation~5):} Primary evaluations were conducted under greedy decoding ($T=0.0$) using \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} and \texttt{databricks-gemma-3-12b}. While setting $T=0.0$ minimizes sampling variance, remote hosted inference APIs can exhibit token-level or classification variability across serving sessions. Across benchmark evaluations, query \texttt{D066} exhibited an empirical classification shift (EASY $\to$ HARD), consistent with numerical or serving-level variability in hosted inference; the precise backend cause cannot be isolated from available logs. Comparing two 14-September TERRA executions across the 350-query benchmark suite, exact string-identical generated answers occurred on \TerraIdenticalAnswerFraction\ of queries overall (206/350), with pronounced category divergence: \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatA\ on Category~A (95/100) and \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatC\ on Category~C (62/75), versus \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatD\ on Category~D (39/75) and \TerraIdenticalAnswerCatB\ on Category~B (10/100). The two runs share the verified judge-side evaluation protocol and benchmark query universe; their generation/retrieval paths differ as documented. Both runs were evaluated under the standardized dual-judge protocol (\texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} and \texttt{databricks-gpt-oss-120b}) using the frozen RAG prompt template (SHA256: \texttt{6d18fc14\dots}) and normalized Likert rubric. Sensitivity verification on an 80B model (\texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct}) across a separate 15-query subset (10 Cat~B, 5 Cat~D; distinct from the firewall stress test in Section~\ref{subsec:benchmark-design}) confirmed invariant relative rankings: TERRA achieved $1.000$ Category~B Faithfulness (vs. $0.900$ Flat RAG, $0.800$ Direct LLM) and $100\%$ Category~D safety rejection (vs. $40\%$ Flat RAG, $0\%$ Direct LLM). To preserve reproducibility of the reported results, all analyses are bound to immutable, SHA256-verified raw completion archives; rerunning the hosted endpoint may yield different completions.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.5.}

\noindent\textbf{Same-Family Generation, NLI Grading, and Category~D Verifier (Limitation~11):} Generation, NLI grading, and the Category~D verifier all deploy \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} (same family and endpoint). Faithfulness judges are \texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} and \texttt{databricks-gpt-oss-120b} (independent families). Category~D four-class labels (refusal, refutation, fatal error, hedge) may inherit shared Llama biases; cross-family verifier ablation has not been run.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.11.}

\noindent\textbf{Mixed-Date Evaluation Blocks (Limitation~13):} Not all blocks were re-evaluated under v2 dual-judge protocols; Supplementary Table S14 details dates and backends. Blocks lacking timestamps (pilot ablation, temporal leakage probe, CaseFacts, CLERC) carry ``date not recorded''; scores derive from earlier single-judge evaluation and are not numerically comparable to v2 evaluations.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.13.}

\noindent\textbf{Oracle Relation Labels, Exact-Title Seeding, and a Bundled Ablation (Limitation~8):} In Full TERRA, curated \texttt{OVERRULES} edges are serialized with an explicit relation tag, dedicated heading, expanded excerpt budget, and prompt instruction; obscure benchmark pairs were drawn from these edges. The Full-TERRA advantage on that suite is therefore contingent on curated annotations, and the bundled ablation cannot isolate the tag alone. For named-case queries, seeding relied on exact caption matches (category-filtered vector retrieval returned no candidates), causing two queries to produce empty context and safe-rated refusals, one to omit the overruling case, and two to take the fast path; we evaluated TERRA as deployed and report sensitivity subsets excluding these items. The primary comparison contrasts complete systems, and Direct LLM receives no instruction block. Outcomes are judge-dependent in magnitude, the suite has thirty items, and judges were not fully blind to arm identity.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.8.}

\noindent\textbf{Citation Extraction Precision, Same-Year Chronology, and Provenance Uncertainty (Limitation~15):} Automated citation extraction via \texttt{eyecite} establishes citation existence rather than doctrinal endorsement. Our stratified audit ($N=\IssueTwentyOneAuditSampleN$, seed \IssueTwentyOneAuditSeed) confirms \IssueTwentyOneAuditCitationPresentPct\ of sampled edges contain reporter strings; direct precedential reliance is verified in \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedPct\ (95\% CI: \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedCI), with \IssueTwentyOneAuditQuotationPct\ in quotations. \textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.15.}

\noindent\textbf{Rule-Based Doctrinal Taxonomy, Lexical Polysemy, Truncation, and Residual Fallback Bias (Limitation~16):} The seven-domain classification is generated by a deterministic \IssueTwentyTwoTotalLexiconPhrases-phrase rule-based lexicon over truncated texts ($\le \IssueTwentyTwoTextTruncationChars$ characters), inducing four limitations: (1)~\textit{Lexical polysemy}: Keyword matching without contextual disambiguation risks misclassification when terms appear in procedural dicta or dissenting quotes. \textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.16.}

\noindent\textbf{A Priori Hyperparameter Selection and Sensitivity Analysis Scope (Limitation~17):} Core retrieval and graph expansion parameters ($k=\IssueTwentyFourSeedK$, depth $d=\IssueTwentyFourBfsDepth$, hub cap $\IssueTwentyFourHubCap$, geometric threshold $\tau=\IssueTwentyFourDistThreshold$) were fixed prior to benchmark construction and evaluation based on topological network constraints and preliminary feasibility testing on an independent \IssueTwentyFourDevQueryCount-query development suite (\IssueTwentyFourDevDate). While this frozen protocol prevents the audited forms of test-set leakage and hyperparameter overfitting, it precludes claiming global parameter optimality. Empirical sensitivity sweeps across \IssueTwentySixConfigCount\ configurations (Section~\ref{subsec:retrieval-quality}, Supplementary Table S10 Panel~C) profile performance across horizons ($k \in \{1,2,4\}$, $d \in \{1,2,3\}$, $C \in \{25,50,100\}$), confirming empirical stability around the historical configuration ($k=2, d=2, C=50$, \IssueTwentySixHistMacro\ macro recall, \IssueTwentySixHistFullPath\ full path recall) while quantifying the coverage-efficiency trade-off under bounded operational caps (\IssueTwentySixGoldRetentionPct\ landmark retention, \IssueTwentySixContextReductionPct\ context reduction).
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.17.}

More fundamentally, we distinguish \textit{latent parametric knowledge} from \textit{operative doctrinal leakage}. Because modern foundation models are pretrained on web-scale text, weights encode post-$T$ legal history (e.g., \textit{Plessy} overruled by \textit{Brown} in 1954). TERRA does not purge latent weights; its provenance-bounded retrieval and temporal gate prevent latent memory from intruding into operative pre-$T$ reasoning. While forensic auditing (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}) confirms suppression of Level-2 leakage in $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$, future work should explore circuit editing and machine unlearning for weight-level guarantees. Provider-side safety filtering on historical legal topics (terminating 85 evaluations in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}) highlights the operational dependency of LLM-as-a-judge pipelines on third-party API policies, motivating our sensitivity-bounded framework. Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization} tests this confounder directly: on obscure overruled precedents Direct LLM safe handling was \ObscDirectSafePct\ (\ObscCrossDirectFamousSafe\ on the famous subset), consistent with famous-landmark performance partly reflecting parametric memory.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.6.}

All \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B false refusals originate from the NLI Smart Grader on the hard route; none occur on the fast route. Individual causes were not separately diagnosed.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.9.}

Aggregate medians obscure this bimodal structure; baseline and TERRA comparisons are indicative only.
\textit{For complete unabridged discussion, see Supplementary Section~S2.10.}

Adding textual refusals (asserting contextual absence without gate triggering) raises counts to \TerraEpistemicRefusals/350 for TERRA, \FlatEpistemicRefusals/350 for Flat Vector RAG, \GraphEpistemicRefusals/350 for GraphRAG-Adapted, and \HippoEpistemicRefusals/350 for HippoRAG-Adapted.
